step.text:
All five are done, typecheck is clean, and it's all renderer-only so HMR shows it immediately. No tests touch these components, and the existing users of the refactored pieces keep their exact APIs.

1. **Agent picker matches the mention list now.** The Do picker uses the same rows as the @mention menu: pet icon, @label, owner name on the right, same glass panel, capped at the same max height (224px) with scrolling. I did it by extracting the mention menu's row into a shared `AgentRow` component, so the two lists can't drift apart. The only difference is highlight source: the mention menu highlights by keyboard index, the picker by hover.

2. **@mentions are stripped from thread titles in the panel.** A thread started from chat as "@Claude fix the bug" now lists as "fix the bug", since the agent name already sits on the line below. I reused the same strip logic the todo composer uses (it became a shared `stripMention` helper), with the same guard: if the title was nothing but the mention, it stays rather than going blank.

3. **Agent hover cards work in the panel.** Hovering an agent name, either the label under a thread row or the @chip under a todo, brings up the same card as chat mentions: icon, provider pill, whose PC, settings. I exported the card wrapper from `Mention.tsx` as `AgentName` so the panel shares one implementation with chat. The name also gets the same subtle hover tint chat mentions have, so it reads as hoverable.

4. **The hover mismatch is fixed.** The row background was on the row's own `:hover` while the action cluster showed on `group-hover`, so pointing at the buttons (which sit in an overlay on top of the row) kept the gradient but dropped the background behind it. The background now keys off `group-hover` too, on all three row types (todos, checked todos, thread rows), so row tint, backing, and gradient always appear and disappear together.

5. **The row stays lit while the picker is open.** Clicking Do on an unassigned todo now pins that row in its hovered state, background on, Delete and Do still showing, until the picker closes. So while you're choosing an agent, it stays obvious which todo you're choosing for, even though your pointer is over the popover.

One inherited detail worth knowing: the picker (like the old one) closes if the panel scrolls, which is standard popover behavior, and the focused state clears with it.

+ import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react'
+ 
+ export type Theme = 'dark' | 'light'
+ 
+ const KEY = 'crew.theme'
+ const listeners = new Set<() => void>()
+ 
+ export function storedTheme(): Theme {
+   return localStorage.getItem(KEY) === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark'
+ }
+ 
+ export function applyTheme(theme: Theme): void {
+   document.documentElement.classList.toggle('light', theme === 'light')
+   localStorage.setItem(KEY, theme)
+   for (const listener of listeners) listener()
+ }
+ 
+ export function useTheme(): Theme {
+   return useSyncExternalStore(listener => {
+     listeners.add(listener)
+     return () => listeners.delete(listener)
+   }, storedTheme)
+ }
+

step.text:
Light mode is in, verified, and synced. Here's what shipped:

**How it works**
- The whole dark palette lives in Tailwind `@theme` variables, so light mode is a single `.light` class on `<html>` that overrides them: `ink-900` becomes straight white, the rest of the ink scale becomes light grays for raised surfaces and borders, `fg` becomes near-black, and `positive`/`danger` deepen to shades that hold contrast on white. Dark mode stays the default and is pixel-identical to before.
- `src/renderer/src/state/theme.ts` owns the decision: stored as `crew.theme` in localStorage (same pattern as `crew.name`), applied before first render, with a `useTheme` hook so components stay in sync when you toggle.
- The toggle is in the profile dropdown: "Light mode" with a sun icon, flipping to "Dark mode" with a moon icon, sitting between Invite link and Leave.

**The tasteful part**
- Every hover, ring, and divider in the app used white-alpha overlays (`bg-white/[0.04]` etc.). I switched them all to `fg`-based (`bg-fg/[0.04]`), which renders identically in dark mode and automatically becomes subtle black overlays on white. No per-component theming needed.
- Hand-tuned light versions for the pieces tokens can't reach: the `.glass` popover (frosted white), scrollbars, text selection, the window's edge ring, focus shadows on inputs and the composer (much softer in light), the tasks panel shadow, the modal scrim, and the BlockNote doc editor, which now follows the app theme instead of being hardcoded dark.
- Per your follow-up on avatars: both `Avatar` and `AgentIcon` now render pale tinted chips in light mode. Same hue per person/pet, but flipped lightness, so a person gets a soft pastel circle with a deeper-toned initial, and the pets sit on pale chips with slightly deepened bodies so they stay vivid on white.

**Verification**: `yarn tsc --noEmit` clean, build clean with the `light:` variant compiled into the bundle, and a new `tests/theme.test.ts` covers default-dark, persistence, and junk-value handling. Full suite passes except the known flaky reconnect timing test, which fails only under full parallel load and passes in isolation (it doesn't touch the renderer). One thing I hit along the way: the doc editor's jsdom test crashed because Node's experimental `localStorage` shadows jsdom's with `undefined`, so theme reads are guarded with `globalThis.localStorage?.`, which is also a sensible guard generally.

Done. Both things you asked for are built, tested, and pushed. All 189 tests pass, typecheck and build are clean.

**Closing the app no longer takes your models away from the crew.** The window closing just hides the app now. The connection to the session, and the CLIs it runs for other people, keep working in the background. On Windows you get a small tray icon in the corner of the taskbar with "Open crew" and "Quit crew", plus a one-time popup explaining that your agents are still shared. On Mac the app stays alive in the dock. Only "Quit crew" actually stops sharing.

**After a restart, opening the app is all you need to do.** The app now remembers the session you were in. On launch it re-hosts (if you were the host) or rejoins (if you joined from a link) automatically, re-detects all your CLIs, and puts your agents back online without you touching anything. You never had to open the CLIs yourself, the app launches them when someone sends a prompt, and now even the joining part is automatic. If you were hosting, your invite link keeps working after the reboot because the session code is stored in the project folder. If the host machine is still off when you open the app, it just keeps retrying quietly until the host comes back.

The only thing that makes the app forget a session is choosing "Leave" from the profile menu. Quitting or restarting the computer never does.

How it works, briefly: the main process saves the session (host or join, folder, name, link) to a small file, restores it on launch, and the renderer shows a short loading state while that happens instead of the home screen. One honest limit remains: the computer has to be on with the app running somewhere (window or background) for others to use your models. If the machine is fully shut down, your agents show offline until you open the app once.

New coverage: `tests/resume.integration.test.ts` boots real servers and proves a host comes back with the same code after a shutdown, a joiner reconnects to the same session, and "Leave" forgets it. Everything is on `main` already, so everyone gets it on their next pull. People will need to restart their app to pick up the new behavior.

title: @Codex Gpt-5.6-sol # Feature Implementation: Studio I want you to build a brand …

text:
@Codex Gpt-5.6-sol # Feature Implementation: Studio



I want you to build a brand new core section of Crew called **Studio**.

This is not a small feature. Studio should become one of the three primary pillars of the application alongside **Chat** and **Docs**.

## Vision

Studio is an AI-native collaborative design workspace.

Think of it as combining:

* Figma's canvas and editing experience
* Claude Artifacts / Stitch's AI UI generation
* Multiplayer collaboration
* Multi-agent AI orchestration

The goal is **not** to copy another product, but to recreate the best design workflow while making it AI-first.

---

# Core Experience

Users should be able to:

* Create unlimited Studio files.
* Organize files from a Studio home page.
* Open any Studio file instantly.
* Collaborate in real time.
* Have multiple AI agents working inside the same Studio simultaneously.
* Design visually.
* Convert designs into production-ready application code.

Studio should feel polished, extremely responsive, and enjoyable to use.

---

# Studio Home

Create a landing page for Studio that acts similarly to a project browser.

Include:

* Recent Studio files
* Shared Studio files
* Favorites
* Templates
* Search
* Create New Studio
* File organization

Every Studio file should autosave.

---

# Canvas

The canvas should feel professional.

Support:

* Rectangle
* Frame
* Circle
* Line
* Arrow
* Text
* Image
* SVG
* Icons
* Components
* Groups
* Layers

Include:

* Infinite canvas
* Zoom
* Pan
* Selection
* Alignment
* Snapping
* Guides
* Grids
* Layer ordering
* Multi-select
* Copy/Paste
* Duplicate
* Lock
* Hide
* Rename

---

# Inspector Panel

The right sidebar should include a complete design inspector.

Support editing:

* Position
* Size
* Rotation
* Opacity
* Fill
* Gradients
* Stroke
* Corner radius
* Shadows
* Blur
* Effects
* Layout
* Auto Layout
* Constraints
* Typography
* Spacing
* Padding
* Alignment
* Colors
* Variables
* Component properties

Everything should update live.

---

# Left Sidebar

Include:

* Layers
* Assets
* Components
* Pages
* File Navigator
* Shared Assets

---

# AI Chat (Studio)

Studio has its own AI chat docked in the bottom-right corner.

The chat supports:

* Images
* Screenshots
* PDFs
* Files
* Drag-and-drop
* Copy/Paste

Users can assign one or many agents.

Examples:

@Codex
@kimi
@Claude

Every selected agent works on the same Studio.

Agents can collaborate together.

---

# AI Design Generation

Users should be able to say things like:

"Design a modern dashboard."

"Create a mobile settings page."

"Build an onboarding flow."

"Design a landing page."

Agents generate the design directly inside Studio.

Nothing opens in a separate window.

Everything appears live on the canvas.

---

# Multiplayer

Studio should support collaborative editing.

Multiple users can:

* Edit simultaneously
* See each other's cursors
* See selections
* Watch live updates
* Add their own agents
* Work on different parts of the same design

This should feel similar to collaborative editing in modern cloud applications.

---

# Multiple AI Agents

Several AI agents can work simultaneously.

Examples:

Agent 1
Designs the dashboard.

Agent 2
Creates icons.

Agent 3
Writes copy.

Agent 4
Builds the design system.

Agent 5
Reviews accessibility.

Users should see live progress for every agent.

---

# Build Animation

While agents are working, show an elegant generation animation.

It should communicate:

* Thinking
* Planning
* Building
* Refining
* Completing

The experience should feel premium and satisfying rather than displaying a static loading spinner.

---

# Design → Code

This is one of the most important features.

Once a design is complete, users can press:

**Build This**

The selected AI agents should convert the Studio design into real production code inside the current repository.

The implementation should preserve:

* Layout
* Components
* Colors
* Assets
* Responsive behavior
* Design structure

The generated code should integrate directly into the existing project.

---

# Chat Integration

Studio should integrate naturally with Chat.

Example:

```
@Codex GPT-5.6-sol /studio

Build me a SaaS dashboard.
```

If Studio doesn't already exist for that request:

* Create a new Studio automatically.
* Redirect the user into it.
* Continue the conversation there.

The transition should feel seamless.

---

# Overall Goal

Studio should become the best place to collaboratively design, prototype, iterate, and build applications with AI.

The experience should combine:

* Professional visual editing
* AI-powered design generation
* Real-time multiplayer collaboration
* Multi-agent orchestration
* Seamless design-to-code workflows

This should feel like a first-class, polished, production-ready feature that fits naturally within Crew and elevates it from an AI chat application into a complete collaborative AI operating system for building software.

+   if ('lineHeight' in raw) patch.lineHeight = num(raw.lineHeight, 0.5, 4, 1.3)
+   if ('letterSpacing' in raw) patch.letterSpacing = num(raw.letterSpacing, -10, 100, 0)
+   if ('flip' in raw) patch.flip = raw.flip === true
+   if ('src' in raw) patch.src = imageSrc(raw.src) ?? null
+   if ('layout' in raw) patch.layout = raw.layout === 'row' || raw.layout === 'column' ? raw.layout : 'none'
+   if ('gap' in raw) patch.gap = num(raw.gap, 0, 1000, 0)
+   if ('padding' in raw) patch.padding = num(raw.padding, 0, 1000, 0)
+   if ('clip' in raw) patch.clip = raw.clip === true
+   return patch
+ }
+ 
+ export function isContainer(node: StudioNode): boolean {
+   return node.type === 'frame' || node.type === 'group'
+ }
+ 
+ export function pageOf(doc: StudioDoc, nodeId: string): StudioPage | undefined {
+   return doc.pages.find(p => p.order.includes(nodeId))
+ }
+ 
+ export function childrenOf(doc: StudioDoc, page: StudioPage, parentId: string | null): StudioNode[] {
+   const out: StudioNode[] = []
+   for (const id of page.order) {
+     const node = doc.nodes[id]
+     if (node && (node.parentId ?? null) === parentId) out.push(node)
+   }
+   return out
+ }
+ 
+ export function descendantsOf(doc: StudioDoc, ids: string[]): Set<string> {
+   const all = new Set(ids.filter(id => doc.nodes[id]))
+   let grew = true
+   while (grew) {
+     grew = false
+     for (const node of Object.values(doc.nodes)) {
+       const parent = node.parentId ?? null
+       if (parent && all.has(parent) && !all.has(node.id)) {
+         all.add(node.id)
+         grew = true
+       }
+     }
+   }
+   return all
+ }
+ 
+ export function absoluteOrigin(doc: StudioDoc, node: StudioNode): { x: number; y: number } {
+   let x = node.x
+   let y = node.y
+   let parentId = node.parentId ?? null
+   let hops = 0
+   while (parentId && hops < 200) {
+     const parent = doc.nodes[parentId]
+     if (!parent) break
+     x += parent.x
+     y += parent.y
+     parentId = parent.parentId ?? null
+     hops++
+   }
+   return { x, y }
+ }
+ 
+ export function rootAncestor(doc: StudioDoc, id: string): string {
+   let current = id
+   let hops = 0
+   while (hops < 200) {
+     const node = doc.nodes[current]
+     const parent = node?.parentId ?? null
+     if (!parent || !doc.nodes[parent]) return current
+     current = parent
+     hops++
+   }
+   return current
+ }
+

+ function compactNode(node: StudioNode): Record<string, unknown> {
+   const out: Record<string, unknown> = {}
+   for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(node)) {
+     if (value === undefined) continue
+     if (key in NODE_DEFAULTS && NODE_DEFAULTS[key] === value) continue
+     if (key === 'src' && typeof value === 'string' && value.startsWith('data:')) {

+ export function serializePage(doc: StudioDoc, page: StudioPage): string {
+   const nodes = page.order.map(id => doc.nodes[id]).filter((n): n is StudioNode => n !== undefined)
+   let json = JSON.stringify(nodes.map(compactNode))
+   if (json.length > PAGE_JSON_LIMIT) {

Config: `/Users/jamel/Documents/Repositories/crew/.yarnrc.yml` | | State | zustand `^5.0.1` | | WebSocket | `ws` `^8.18.0` (server), native `WebSocket` (renderer) | | Styling | Tailwind CSS `^4.0.0` via `@tailwindcss/vite` | | Tests | vitest `^2.1.4` + jsdom + @testing-library/react | **Editor / canvas libraries already present:** - **BlockNote** — `@blocknote/core`, `@blocknote/mantine`, `@blocknote/react` (all `^0.51.4`) — block-based rich text editor (the Docs editor). - **Mantine** — `@mantine/core`, `@mantine/hooks` (`^8.3.11`) — pulled in by BlockNote. - `marked` `^12.0.2` + `dompurify` `^3.1.6` — markdown rendering for chat (`components/Markdown.tsx`). - `@heroicons/react` `^2.2.0` — icons. **No canvas/whiteboard/diagram/collab library** is installed: no tldraw, excalidraw, fabric, konva, react-flow, Yjs, or `` abstraction. Docs call `emit(..., { persist: false })` — they broadcast live but are NOT written to the event log (the markdown file is the source of truth instead). --- ## 5. Per-feature persistence under `.crew/` and git sync Persistence is centralized in **`/Users/jamel/Documents/Repositories/crew/src/server/store.ts`** (`Store`, rooted at `/.crew`, created in the constructor `store.ts:26-30`). Wired in **`/Users/jamel/Documents/Repositories/crew/src/main/session.ts:183-185`**: ```ts const git = new GitSync(repoPath) session.onSyncNeeded = () => git.schedule() ``` - `schedule()` debounces 2s (`git.ts:11-14`); `syncNow()` runs a serialized promise chain (`:20-23`): `git add -A` → if staged, `git commit -m "crew sync"` → if a remote exists, `git pull --rebase` → `git push` (`:25-52`). - **Conflict handling (`git.ts:57-78`)**: during rebase, if the *only* conflicted files are `session.json`, it resolves them with `checkout --theirs` and continues; any other conflicted file aborts the rebase and leaves it. **`.gitattributes` (`/Users/jamel/Documents/Repositories/crew/.gitattributes`): `*.jsonl merge=union`** — so `chat.jsonl` auto-merges via union (append-only logs concatenate cleanly). `.md` docs have **no special merge driver**, so concurrent edits to the same doc page can hit a normal git text conflict that aborts the rebase — reinforcing that the current model is single-writer-per-doc. `.gitignore` excludes `node_modules/ out/ dist/ .DS_Store` — `.crew/` **is** committed. --- ## Summary of the key seams for a collaborative "Design" canvas - **Tab wiring:** `TopBar.tsx` (`Tab` union + `TABS`), `App.tsx` (`

# Crew agent execution pipeline — map for a shared live-canvas feature

Crew is an Electron app. One person **hosts** (runs the WS server + a runner) and others **join** (runner only). Agents are local LLM CLIs (`claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `kimi`) wrapped as providers. Everything durable is persisted under `.crew/` and synced via git. There is **no existing canvas/cursor/typing/presence-broadcast concept** — I grepped; the only "ephemeral" plumbing is doc events and live agent steps (details in §4).

## 1. src/runner — prompt in, stream out, files

**How a prompt reaches a CLI.** The server sends a `prompt` WS message; the runner routes it per-thread and spawns the CLI:
- `src/runner/index.ts:258` `handle()` → `case 'prompt'` → `runPrompt()` (`:328`) serializes runs per `threadId` via a promise `tails` chain (`:343`) → `execute()` (`:354`).
- `execute()` (`:354-384`): `await this.puller?.pullNow()` first (join mode only), fetches attachments, then `provider.start(promptWithAttachments(text, local), this.opts.repoPath, { onStep, onTokens }, settings)` (`:370`). The prompt text and `repoPath` (cwd) are the only inputs; settings are `{model, effort}` strings.

**Provider adapters.** All CLIs are built by one factory:
- `src/runner/providers/cli.ts:74` `makeCliProvider()`. It `spawn`s the CLI (`:90`) with `cwd`, `detached`, and stdio. Two input modes:
  - **argv mode** (codex): prompt passed as last arg — `src/runner/providers/codex.ts:127` `codexArgs` ends with `prompt`.
  - **stream-json stdin mode** (claude): prompt written to stdin as JSON, stdin kept open for steering — `src/runner/providers/claude.ts:84` `claudeArgs` (`--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`), and `cli.ts:140` `writeMessage()` writes `{type:'user',message:{role:'user',content:[{type:'text',text}]}}`. `streamInput:true` ⇒ `steerable:true` (`cli.ts:80`).
- `Provider` interface: `src/runner/providers/types.ts:41`. Adapters: `claude.ts`, `codex.ts`, `grok.ts`, `kimi.ts`; registry in `src/runner/providers/detect.ts`.

**How streaming comes back.** Each provider has an `OutputParser` (`types.ts:24`) turning CLI stdout lines into `ParsedOutput[]` (`types.ts:12`). `cli.ts:197` `handleLine()` maps those to `hooks.onStep(RunStep)` / `hooks.onTokens(n)`. In `index.ts:371-372` those hooks become `agent.step` / `agent.tokens` client messages. Final result resolves `run.done` → `agent.done` (`index.ts:377`).
- Claude parser: `claude.ts:9` `parseClaudeLine` handles `stream_event` (thinking deltas), `assistant` blocks (`text`, `thinking`, `tool_use`), `result` (turn end + tokens).
- Codex parser: `codex.ts:61` `parseCodexLine` handles `item.*` events (`agent_message`, `reasoning`, tool items).

**Structured output / tool calls — important for canvas.** There is **no mechanism to give the agent tools or request structured output.** The prompt is plain prose (`buildPrompt`, §2). Crew only *parses tool use out of* the CLI's own stream:
- `ParsedActivity` (`types.ts:3`) with `kind: 'tool' | 'subagent'` and `files?: FileChange[]`.
- File edits are reconstructed from tool inputs by `src/runner/providers/detail.ts:38` `fileChanges()` (reads `file_path`/`old_string`/`new_string`/`content`, builds a `+/-` diff). Claude maps `tool_use` blocks at `claude.ts:42-53`; codex maps `file_change` items at `codex.ts:90-99`.
- **Steering** is the one channel to push data into a live run: `cli.ts:140` `writeMessage()` (claude only). The runner frames it as `New message from ${byName}:\n${text}` (`index.ts:317`). A canvas "tool call" today would have to be either (a) parsed out of the agent's file writes/stdout, or (b) injected as steer text — there is no JSON tool protocol to extend.

**How the runner reads/writes files.** It doesn't edit repo files itself — it runs the CLI with `cwd = repoPath` and permission bypass so the *CLI* edits files directly:
- `claude.ts:95` `'--permission-mode','bypassPermissions','--dangerously-skip-permissions'`; `codex.ts:129` `'--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox'`.
- Only runner-owned file writes are attachment caching (`src/runner/attachments.ts:15` writes to `.crew/attachments`) and git pulls (`src/runner/pull.ts`).

## 2. src/server — session state, chat, threads, @mentions, broadcast

**Session state shape** — `src/server/session.ts:114` `CrewSession`. In-memory maps: `members` (`:117`), `agents` (`:118`, `AgentState` at `:40`), `threads` (`:119`, `Thread` at `:82`), `todos`, `events` (`SessionEvent[]`, `:121`), `docs`, `prompts` (promptId→{agentId,threadId,messageId}, `:126`), `steers` (`:127`). The wire snapshot is `SessionSnapshot` (`src/shared/protocol.ts:30`): `{code, members, agents (PooledAgent[]), events, docs, queues, todos}`. Persisted to `.crew/` by `src/server/store.ts` (`session.json`, `chat.jsonl`, `docs/*.md`).

**Agent messages in chat.** Everything is a `SessionEvent` (`src/shared/events.ts:20`). A run emits `agent.start` → `agent.step`* → `agent.end` (`events.ts:54-56`). The renderer turns these into chat items in `src/renderer/src/components/thread.ts:119` `buildThread()` — steps render as `reply`/`thinking`/`tool` items under their `agent.start`. Live steps are held in `AgentState.runs` (`session.ts:47` `RunState.steps`) and only persisted as events when `status==='done'` (`session.ts:860` `persistStep`).

**Threads + @mentions routing.** `handleChat` (`session.ts:401`):
- No thread + mentions ⇒ `startThread()` per mentioned agent (`:440`, `:459`).
- Inside a thread ⇒ mentions pick the target agent(s); `switchThreadAgent` (`:443`) reassigns, `enqueuePrompt` (`:966`) queues.
- Mention parsing: `src/shared/llm.ts:133` `mentionsIn()` matches `@label` against online agents (client computes it in `state/store.ts:413` before `chat.send`; server re-filters to known agents at `session.ts:415`).
- `enqueuePrompt` (`:966`) has the key routing decision: if the mentioned agent **is already running in this thread and is steerable**, the message is folded into the live run via `sendSteer` (`:996-1006`, `:1029`); otherwise it's queued and `runThread()` (`:1085`) dispatches `{type:'prompt'}` to that agent's runner socket (`:1109`).
- Agent↔runner binding: `AgentState.runner` is the WS of the owning runner; `registerAgent` (`:1198`) sets it. `agentId = owner/instanceId`.

**Broadcast to all clients.** `session.ts:1383` `broadcast()` iterates `this.meta` and sends to every `role==='ui'` socket. `emit()` (`:1370`) is the single funnel: pushes to `events`, appends to store, then broadcasts `{type:'event', event}`. Non-event live data uses direct `broadcast()` calls: `agent.step` (`:834`,`:848`), `agent.tokens` (`:808`), `queue.state` (`:1026`), `agent.added/removed/usage`. The WS server + client set live in `src/server/index.ts:94-118` (upgrade handler adds sockets to `clients`; `session.attach(ws)` at `:116`).

**This is the seam for canvas events.** A new `canvas.*` client→server message added to `ClientMessage` (`protocol.ts:40`) + a `handleMessage` case (`session.ts:312`) + a `broadcast()` server→client message (`protocol.ts:70`) is exactly how `queue.state`/`agent.step` already work.

## 3. How agents edit shared state beyond chat text

**Docs are NOT agent-editable live.** Docs live as files at `.crew/docs/*.md` (`store.ts:95` `saveDoc`, serialized with title frontmatter by `src/shared/docs.ts:94`). But the authoritative `this.docs` map only updates from **UI** `doc.update`/`doc.rename`/etc. messages (`session.ts:623` `handleDoc`, dispatched at `:345`) — driven by the human `DocEditor` (BlockNote) at `src/renderer/src/components/DocEditor.tsx`. If an agent wrote a `.crew/docs/*.md` file directly, the server would not broadcast a `doc` event; it'd only be picked up on next restart via `store.loadDocs()` (`session.ts:243`). So docs are a human-authoritative model, **not** the pattern to copy for agent-driven live edits.

**Agents edit real repo files** (code), via the bypass-permission CLI (§1). Those surface as `FileChange` steps in the thread and a diff summary (`src/renderer/src/views/ThreadView.tsx:72` `diffTotals`, `FilesChanged` component).

**Auto-commit/push flow.** `src/server/git.ts:3` `GitSync`:
- Wired in `src/main/session.ts:185` `session.onSyncNeeded = () => git.schedule()`. `onSyncNeeded` fires from every persisted `emit()` (`session.ts:1380`) and from doc handlers.
- `schedule()` debounces 2s (`git.ts:11`) → `sync()` (`:25`): `git add -A` (sweeps up **all** agent file edits), commit `"crew sync"`, `pull --rebase` (auto-resolves `session.json` conflicts with `--theirs`, `:57`), `push`.
- **Asymmetry worth knowing for a shared canvas:** `GitSync` is created **only in `startHost`** (`main/session.ts:183`). Joiners get only a `GitPuller` (`main/session.ts:224`, `runner/pull.ts` — pull `--rebase --autostash`, no push). So agent file edits flow host→joiners reliably, but a **joiner-owned** agent's file writes are not auto-committed/pushed. A live canvas should not ride git for real-time state; it should use a new WS message (§2), with git only as durable backup like docs.

## 4. Presence / ephemeral messaging

**Existing "broadcast but not persisted" patterns** (closest thing to what you want):
- **Doc events** — `session.ts:1370` `emit()` treats `doc`, `doc.titled`, `doc.renamed`, `doc.deleted`, `message.edited` as `ephemeral`: not pushed to in-memory `events`, and doc handlers call `emit(..., {persist:false})` so they're **not written to chat.jsonl** either — pure broadcast, durable state lives in the file. Also `EPHEMERAL_KINDS` in `src/shared/events.ts:70` keeps them out of the snapshot window.
- **Live agent steps** — running steps are broadcast (`session.ts:848` `broadcastStep`, throttled `STEP_FLUSH_MS=80` at `:112`) but only persisted on `done`.
- **`agent.tokens`** — broadcast, never persisted (`session.ts:802`).
- Server heartbeat `{type:'ping'}` (`src/server/index.ts:134`).

There is **no typing indicator and no agent-status broadcast** ("working" is derived, not pushed). A canvas cursor stream would be a brand-new ephemeral type modeled on doc events / `agent.tokens`.

**How "agent is working" shows today** (all derived from `agent.start`/`agent.end`, i.e. `threadPrompts`/`activePrompts` in `state/store.ts:36-38`):
- Thread header: `ThreadView.tsx:171` — `state==='working'` renders `<Spinner/> Working`. `threadState()` at `thread.ts:19` returns `'working'` when a prompt is running.
- Live status line: `src/renderer/src/components/RunStatus.tsx` — spinner + `describeStep(last)` (`thread.ts:67`: "Thinking"/"Writing"/tool name) + elapsed + tokens.
- Chat list cards: `Chat.tsx:79` `threadStatus()`; `AgentCard.tsx:23` `status = threadCount>0 ? 'busy' : agent.status`; `ThreadCard.tsx:21` spinner when working.
- Agent status enum `idle|busy|offline` computed server-side in `session.ts:1296` `statusOf()` from `runner`+`running.size`.

## 5. Agent identity (for attributing a canvas cursor)

- **Canonical id**: `src/shared/llm.ts:113` `agentId(ownerName, instanceId)` = `` `${owner.toLowerCase()}/${instanceId}` ``. Stable across reconnects; set at `session.ts:1199`.
- **`PooledAgent`** (`llm.ts:83`) is the full identity broadcast to clients: `{id, label, provider, ownerId, ownerName, status, settings, fields, steerable, usage, runs}`. Built by `session.ts:1301` `pooled()`, shipped in the snapshot and via `agent.added` (`:1233`).
- **Visual identity / icon seed**: `AgentIcon` (`src/renderer/src/components/AgentIcon.tsx`) generates a deterministic "pet" blob + hue from a **`seed` string**. Every call site passes **`seed={agent.id}`** (e.g. `ChatMessage.tsx:70` via `agentSeed = agents.find(a=>a.label===item.author)?.id`; `ThreadView.tsx:166` `seed={thread.agentId}`; `MentionPicker.tsx:81`; `Mention.tsx:21`). Per AGENTS.md:35, "Agents always render `AgentIcon` (a deterministic generated pet seeded by the agent id)." Humans use `Avatar` (seeded by name, `Avatar.tsx:15`).
- So a canvas cursor attributed to agent X should carry **`agentId`** and render `<AgentIcon seed={agentId} .../>` with `agent.label` for the name — identical to how threads/messages attribute agents today. The color hue is derivable from the same seed if you want cursor color to match the icon (`AgentIcon.tsx:97` `petOf(seed).hue`).

---

### The concrete seams you'd hook into
| Concern | File:line | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Add canvas WS message types | `src/shared/protocol.ts:40` (Client) / `:70` (Server) | mirror `queue.state`/`agent.step` |
| Route/handle canvas messages, hold state | `src/server/session.ts:312` dispatch, add map beside `docs`/`threads` | |
| Broadcast to all UIs | `src/server/session.ts:1383` `broadcast()`; ephemeral pattern at `:1370` `emit(...,{persist:false})` | |
| Include canvas in snapshot | `src/shared/protocol.ts:30` `SessionSnapshot` + `session.ts:276` `snapshot()` | |
| Inject canvas actions/data into a live agent | `src/runner/index.ts:311` `steer()` / `providers/cli.ts:140` `writeMessage` (claude, steerable) | only text channel today |
| Surface agent file/tool actions (if canvas is file-backed) | `src/runner/providers/detail.ts:38` `fileChanges`, `claude.ts:42`, `codex.ts:90` | |
| Client state + WS handling | `src/renderer/src/state/store.ts:270` `handleMessage`, `api/ws.ts` | |
| Attribute cursor to agent | `agentId` (`shared/llm.ts:113`), `PooledAgent` (`shared/llm.ts:83`), `AgentIcon seed={agent.id}` | |
| Durable backup (optional) | `src/server/store.ts` + `src/server/git.ts` `git add -A` auto-commit | host-only push |

# Design tab plan

**Recommendation in one line:** build the canvas on the tldraw SDK (v4), sync it over crew's existing websocket with the server as authority, persist boards to `.crew/designs/` like docs, and give agents a small HTTP "canvas API" on the host so they can read and edit the board live, with their pet-icon cursors animating as their edits land.

## Why tldraw

- It's the highest fidelity Figma-like canvas you can get off the shelf: infinite canvas, frames, shapes, text, arrows, images, snapping, alignment, styles panel, zoom and pan. Excalidraw is MIT but looks hand-drawn, and building on Konva from scratch would take months to reach this polish.
- It has a full programmatic Editor and Store API (`createShapes`, `updateShapes`, record-level diffs), which is exactly what agent-driven edits need. tldraw even ships an [agent starter kit](https://tldraw.dev/starter-kits/agent) with streaming canvas edits and a chat panel, which we can crib patterns from.
- Native multiplayer presence: it renders collaborator cursors and selections from presence records out of the box, so live cursors are mostly wiring, not custom rendering.
- Compatible with our stack: React 18.3, Vite, works fine in Electron.
- One catch: the free tier shows a small "made with tldraw" watermark on the canvas, removable with a paid [business license](https://tldraw.dev/legal/tldraw-license). I'd ship with the watermark and decide later.

## Sync architecture

We don't need tldraw's hosted sync. Crew already has the right plumbing, and doc events prove the pattern (broadcast live, file is source of truth, nothing in chat.jsonl).

- **Wire:** new `design.*` message types in `src/shared/protocol.ts`. Client listens to its tldraw store for document diffs and sends `design.apply { boardId, changes }`. The server applies them to an authoritative in-memory board, broadcasts to everyone else, and clients merge with `store.mergeRemoteChanges`. Record-level last-writer-wins, which is the same model Figma itself uses. No CRDT needed.
- **Presence:** ephemeral `design.presence` messages (pointer, selection, camera), broadcast and never persisted, modeled on `agent.tokens`. Clients turn them into tldraw presence records, so cursors, names, and selection highlights render natively.
- **Persistence:** server debounce-writes each board as a tldraw snapshot to `.crew/designs/<slug>.json` using the existing atomic-write pattern, and `onSyncNeeded` lets GitSync commit it. Only the host server writes these files, so no merge conflicts. Boards load lazily (`design.open` returns the snapshot, then diffs stream), so the welcome payload stays small.

## Agents on the canvas

This is the headline feature, and the runner mapping surfaced the key constraint: there is no tool or structured-output protocol today, agents are CLIs running with the repo as cwd. So instead of parsing canvas commands out of chat text, we give agents a real API:

- **Canvas HTTP API on the host server** (it already serves HTTP for attachments, and joiner runners already reach it): `GET /design/:board` returns the board as simple JSON, `POST /design/:board/ops` accepts a batch of ops (`create`, `update`, `move`, `delete`, `style`, with shape types mapped to tldraw records). The server validates, applies, broadcasts, and responds with results and new shape ids, so agents get error feedback and can self-correct. Since the CLIs can run bash, `curl` is the whole client.
- **Prompt preamble:** when a prompt is dispatched for a thread attached to a design board, the server prepends a short spec of the API plus the current selection and board summary. That's a change at the prompt-dispatch seam in `session.ts`, no provider adapter changes needed.
- **Agent cursors:** the server synthesizes `design.presence` for the agent id from its ops, gliding the cursor to each shape it touches, and clients tween the motion. You'll see the pet icon (`AgentIcon` seeded by agent id, cursor tinted with the same hue) moving around the board as shapes appear, without depending on the agent to send cursor moves. Agents can also set their cursor explicitly through the API.
- **Design chat:** a right-side panel inside the Design view, reusing `Composer`, thread rendering, and `RunStatus`. You @mention an agent, your current selection rides along as context, and the reply streams while the board updates live. Same thread model as chat, just scoped to the board.

## UI

- New `design` entry in the `Tab` union, `TABS`, and the `TabIcon` map (it's exhaustive, so it won't compile without the icon), plus `views/Design.tsx`. Lazy-load the view with a dynamic import since tldraw is a heavy dependency and Chat startup shouldn't pay for it.
- Board list sidebar matching the Docs page tree: create, rename, delete, boards stored flat under `.crew/designs/`.
- tldraw's dark theme restyled with our ink tokens so it sits flush with the rest of the app. Keep tldraw's own toolbar and style panel for fidelity, they're already the Figma-like part.
- Humans get colored cursors with name labels, agents get pet cursors. A small avatar row in the view chrome shows who's on the board.

## Build phases

1. **Canvas:** tab wiring, Design view, board list, tldraw mounted, server-side board state and persistence, single user. Integration tests for board CRUD and snapshot persistence.
2. **Multiplayer:** diff sync and presence over ws. Tests boot the real server with two ws clients and assert diffs and cursors propagate and that presence stays out of chat.jsonl.
3. **Agents:** canvas HTTP API, prompt preamble, synthesized agent presence, design chat panel. Tests drive the API directly and assert ops broadcast and agent cursors emit.
4. **Polish:** cursor tweening, selection context in prompts, PNG export, theming pass, license decision.

Two things to flag before implementation starts: the watermark question above, and the fact that this repo is live with other agents, so whoever implements should claim the `TopBar`/`App` seam in chat first to avoid collisions. Want me to start on phase 1?

In-memory maps: `members` (`:117`), `agents` (`:118`, `AgentState` at `:40`), `threads` (`:119`, `Thread` at `:82`), `todos`, `events` (`SessionEvent[]`, `:121`), `docs`, `prompts` (promptId→{agentId,threadId,messageId}, `:126`), `steers` (`:127`). The wire snapshot is `SessionSnapshot` (`src/shared/protocol.ts:30`): `{code, members, agents (PooledAgent[]), events, docs, queues, todos}`. Persisted to `.crew/` by `src/server/store.ts` (`session.json`, `chat.jsonl`, `docs/*.md`). **Agent messages in chat.** Everything is a `SessionEvent` (`src/shared/events.ts:20`). A run emits `agent.start` → `agent.step`* → `agent.end` (`events.ts:54-56`). The renderer turns these into chat items in `src/renderer/src/components/thread.ts:119` `buildThread()` — steps render as `reply`/`thinking`/`tool` items under their `agent.start`. Live steps are held in `AgentState.runs` (`session.ts:47` `RunState.steps`) and only persisted as events when `status==='done'` (`session.ts:860` `persistStep`). **Threads + @mentions routing.** `handleChat` (`session.ts:401`): - No thread + mentions ⇒ `startThread()` per mentioned agent (`:440`, `:459`). - Inside a thread ⇒ mentions pick the target agent(s); `switchThreadAgent` (`:443`) reassigns, `enqueuePrompt` (`:966`) queues. - Mention parsing: `src/shared/llm.ts:133` `mentionsIn()` matches `@label` against online agents (client computes it in `state/store.ts:413` before `chat.send`; server re-filters to known agents at `session.ts:415`). - `enqueuePrompt` (`:966`) has the key routing decision: if the mentioned agent **is already running in this thread and is steerable**, the message is folded into the live run via `sendSteer` (`:996-1006`, `:1029`); otherwise it's queued and `runThread()` (`:1085`) dispatches `{type:'prompt'}` to that agent's runner socket (`:1109`). - Agent↔runner binding: `AgentState.runner` is the WS of the owning runner; `registerAgent` (`:1198`) sets it. `agentId = owner/instanceId`. **Broadcast to all clients.** `session.ts:1383` `broadcast()` iterates `this.meta` and sends to every `role==='ui'` socket. `emit()` (`:1370`) is the single funnel: pushes to `events`, appends to store, then broadcasts `{type:'event', event}`. Non-event live data uses direct `broadcast()` calls: `agent.step` (`:834`,`:848`), `agent.tokens` (`:808`), `queue.state` (`:1026`), `agent.added/removed/usage`. The WS server + client set live in `src/server/index.ts:94-118` (upgrade handler adds sockets to `clients`; `session.attach(ws)` at `:116`). **This is the seam for canvas events.** A new `canvas.*` client→server message added to `ClientMessage` (`protocol.ts:40`) + a `handleMessage` case (`session.ts:312`) + a `broadcast()` server→client message (`protocol.ts:70`) is exactly how `queue.state`/`agent.step` already work. ## 3. How agents edit shared state beyond chat text **Docs are NOT agent-editable live.** Docs live as files at `.crew/docs/*.md` (`store.ts:95` `saveDoc`, serialized with title frontmatter by `src/shared/docs.ts:94`). But the authoritative `this.docs` map only updates from **UI** `doc.update`/`doc.rename`/etc. messages (`session.ts:623` `handleDoc`, dispatched at `:345`) — driven by the human `DocEditor` (BlockNote) at `src/renderer/src/components/DocEditor.tsx`. If an agent wrote a `.crew/docs/*.md` file directly, the server would not broadcast a `doc` event; it'd only be picked up on next restart via `store.loadDocs()` (`session.ts:243`). So docs are a human-authoritative model, **not** the pattern to copy for agent-driven live edits. **Agents edit real repo files** (code), via the bypass-permission CLI (§1). Those surface as `FileChange` steps in the thread and a diff summary (`src/renderer/src/views/ThreadView.tsx:72` `diffTotals`, `FilesChanged` component). **Auto-commit/push flow.** `src/server/git.ts:3` `GitSync`: - Wired in `src/main/session.ts:185` `session.onSyncNeeded = () => git.schedule()`. `onSyncNeeded` fires from every persisted `emit()` (`session.ts:1380`) and from doc handlers. - `schedule()` debounces 2s (`git.ts:11`) → `sync()` (`:25`): `git add -A` (sweeps up **all** agent file edits), commit `"crew sync"`, `pull --rebase` (auto-resolves `session.json` conflicts with `--theirs`, `:57`), `push`. - **Asymmetry worth knowing for a shared canvas:** `GitSync` is created **only in `startHost`** (`main/session.ts:183`). Joiners get only a `GitPuller` (`main/session.ts:224`, `runner/pull.ts` — pull `--rebase --autostash`, no push). So agent file edits flow host→joiners reliably, but a **joiner-owned** agent's file writes are not auto-committed/pushed. A live canvas should not ride git for real-time state; it should use a new WS message (§2), with git only as durable backup like docs. ## 4. Presence / ephemeral messaging **Existing "broadcast but not persisted" patterns** (closest thing to what you want): - **Doc events** — `session.ts:1370` `emit()` treats `doc`, `doc.titled`, `doc.renamed`, `doc.deleted`, `message.edited` as `ephemeral`: not pushed to in-memory `events`, and doc handlers call `emit(..., {persist:false})` so they're **not written to chat.jsonl** either — pure broadcast, durable state lives in the file. Also `EPHEMERAL_KINDS` in `src/shared/events.ts:70` keeps them out of the snapshot window. - **Live agent steps** — running steps are broadcast (`session.ts:848` `broadcastStep`, throttled `STEP_FLUSH_MS=80` at `:112`) but only persisted on `done`. - **`agent.tokens`** — broadcast, never persisted (`session.ts:802`). - Server heartbeat `{type:'ping'}` (`src/server/index.ts:134`). There is **no typing indicator and no agent-status broadcast** ("working" is derived, not pushed). A canvas cursor stream would be a brand-new ephemeral type modeled on doc events / `agent.tokens`. **How "agent is working" shows today** (all derived from `agent.start`/`agent.end`, i.e. `threadPrompts`/`activePrompts` in `state/store.ts:36-38`): - Thread header: `ThreadView.tsx:171` — `state==='working'` renders ` Working`. `threadState()` at `thread.ts:19` returns `'working'` when a prompt is running. - Live status line: `src/renderer/src/components/RunStatus.tsx` — spinner + `describeStep(last)` (`thread.ts:67`: "Thinking"/"Writing"/tool name) + elapsed + tokens. - Chat list cards: `Chat.tsx:79` `threadStatus()`; `AgentCard.tsx:23` `status = threadCount>0 ? 'busy' : agent.status`; `ThreadCard.tsx:21` spinner when working. - Agent status enum `idle|busy|offline` computed server-side in `session.ts:1296` `statusOf()` from `runner`+`running.size`. ## 5. Agent identity (for attributing a canvas cursor) - **Canonical id**: `src/shared/llm.ts:113` `agentId(ownerName, instanceId)` = `` `${owner.toLowerCase()}/${instanceId}` ``. Stable across reconnects; set at `session.ts:1199`. - **`PooledAgent`** (`llm.ts:83`) is the full identity broadcast to clients: `{id, label, provider, ownerId, ownerName, status, settings, fields, steerable, usage, runs}`. Built by `session.ts:1301` `pooled()`, shipped in the snapshot and via `agent.added` (`:1233`). - **Visual identity / icon seed**: `AgentIcon` (`src/renderer/src/components/AgentIcon.tsx`) generates a deterministic "pet" blob + hue from a **`seed` string**. Every call site passes **`seed={agent.id}`** (e.g. `ChatMessage.tsx:70` via `agentSeed = agents.find(a=>a.label===item.author)?.id`; `ThreadView.tsx:166` `seed={thread.agentId}`; `MentionPicker.tsx:81`; `Mention.tsx:21`). Per AGENTS.md:35, "Agents always render `AgentIcon` (a deterministic generated pet seeded by the agent id)." Humans use `Avatar` (seeded by name, `Avatar.tsx:15`). - So a canvas cursor attributed to agent X should carry **`agentId`** and render `` with `agent.label` for the name — identical to how threads/messages attribute agents today. The color hue is derivable from the same seed if you want cursor color to match the icon (`AgentIcon.tsx:97` `petOf(seed).hue`). --- ### The concrete seams you'd hook into | Concern | File:line | Note | |---|---|---| | Add canvas WS message types | `src/shared/protocol.ts:40` (Client) / `:70` (Server) | mirror `queue.state`/`agent.step` | | Route/handle canvas messages, hold state | `src/server/session.ts:312` dispatch, add map beside `docs`/`threads` | | | Broadcast to all UIs | `src/server/session.ts:1383` `broadcast()`; ephemeral pattern at `:1370` `emit(...,{persist:false})` | | | Include canvas in snapshot | `src/shared/protocol.ts:30` `SessionSnapshot` + `session.ts:276` `snapshot()` | | | Inject canvas actions/data into a live agent | `src/runner/index.ts:311` `steer()` / `providers/cli.ts:140` `writeMessage` (claude, steerable) | only text channel today | | Surface agent file/tool actions (if canvas is file-backed) | `src/runner/providers/detail.ts:38` `fileChanges`, `claude.ts:42`, `codex.ts:90` | | | Client state + WS handling | `src/renderer/src/state/store.ts:270` `handleMessage`, `api/ws.ts` | | | Attribute cursor to agent | `agentId` (`shared/llm.ts:113`), `PooledAgent` (`shared/llm.ts:83`), `AgentIcon seed={agent.id}` | | | Durable backup (optional) | `src/server/store.ts` + `src/server/git.ts` `git add -A` auto-commit | host-only push | Both explorers are back, and the codebase mapping confirms this is very buildable on crew's existing seams. Here's the plan. # Design tab plan **Recommendation in one line:** build the canvas on the tldraw SDK (v4), sync it over crew's existing websocket with the server as authority, persist boards to `.crew/designs/` like docs, and give agents a small HTTP "canvas API" on the host so they can read and edit the board live, with their pet-icon cursors animating as their edits land. ## Why tldraw - It's the highest fidelity Figma-like canvas you can get off the shelf: infinite canvas, frames, shapes, text, arrows, images, snapping, alignment, styles panel, zoom and pan. Excalidraw is MIT but looks hand-drawn, and building on Konva from scratch would take months to reach this polish. - It has a full programmatic Editor and Store API (`createShapes`, `updateShapes`, record-level diffs), which is exactly what agent-driven edits need. tldraw even ships an [agent starter kit](https://tldraw.dev/starter-kits/agent) with streaming canvas edits and a chat panel, which we can crib patterns from. - Native multiplayer presence: it renders collaborator cursors and selections from presence records out of the box, so live cursors are mostly wiring, not custom rendering. - Compatible with our stack: React 18.3, Vite, works fine in Electron. - One catch: the free tier shows a small "made with tldraw" watermark on the canvas, removable with a paid [business license](https://tldraw.dev/legal/tldraw-license). I'd ship with the watermark and decide later. ## Sync architecture We don't need tldraw's hosted sync. Crew already has the right plumbing, and doc events prove the pattern (broadcast live, file is source of truth, nothing in chat.jsonl). - **Wire:** new `design.*` message types in `src/shared/protocol.ts`. Client listens to its tldraw store for document diffs and sends `design.apply { boardId, changes }`. The server applies them to an authoritative in-memory board, broadcasts to everyone else, and clients merge with `store.mergeRemoteChanges`. Record-level last-writer-wins, which is the same model Figma itself uses. No CRDT needed. - **Presence:** ephemeral `design.presence` messages (pointer, selection, camera), broadcast and never persisted, modeled on `agent.tokens`. Clients turn them into tldraw presence records, so cursors, names, and selection highlights render natively. - **Persistence:** server debounce-writes each board as a tldraw snapshot to `.crew/designs/.json` using the existing atomic-write pattern, and `onSyncNeeded` lets GitSync commit it. Only the host server writes these files, so no merge conflicts. Boards load lazily (`design.open` returns the snapshot, then diffs stream), so the welcome payload stays small. ## Agents on the canvas This is the headline feature, and the runner mapping surfaced the key constraint: there is no tool or structured-output protocol today, agents are CLIs running with the repo as cwd. So instead of parsing canvas commands out of chat text, we give agents a real API: - **Canvas HTTP API on the host server** (it already serves HTTP for attachments, and joiner runners already reach it): `GET /design/:board` returns the board as simple JSON, `POST /design/:board/ops` accepts a batch of ops (`create`, `update`, `move`, `delete`, `style`, with shape types mapped to tldraw records). The server validates, applies, broadcasts, and responds with results and new shape ids, so agents get error feedback and can self-correct. Since the CLIs can run bash, `curl` is the whole client. - **Prompt preamble:** when a prompt is dispatched for a thread attached to a design board, the server prepends a short spec of the API plus the current selection and board summary. That's a change at the prompt-dispatch seam in `session.ts`, no provider adapter changes needed. - **Agent cursors:** the server synthesizes `design.presence` for the agent id from its ops, gliding the cursor to each shape it touches, and clients tween the motion. You'll see the pet icon (`AgentIcon` seeded by agent id, cursor tinted with the same hue) moving around the board as shapes appear, without depending on the agent to send cursor moves. Agents can also set their cursor explicitly through the API. - **Design chat:** a right-side panel inside the Design view, reusing `Composer`, thread rendering, and `RunStatus`. You @mention an agent, your current selection rides along as context, and the reply streams while the board updates live. Same thread model as chat, just scoped to the board. ## UI - New `design` entry in the `Tab` union, `TABS`, and the `TabIcon` map (it's exhaustive, so it won't compile without the icon), plus `views/Design.tsx`. Lazy-load the view with a dynamic import since tldraw is a heavy dependency and Chat startup shouldn't pay for it. - Board list sidebar matching the Docs page tree: create, rename, delete, boards stored flat under `.crew/designs/`. - tldraw's dark theme restyled with our ink tokens so it sits flush with the rest of the app. Keep tldraw's own toolbar and style panel for fidelity, they're already the Figma-like part. - Humans get colored cursors with name labels, agents get pet cursors. A small avatar row in the view chrome shows who's on the board. ## Build phases 1. **Canvas:** tab wiring, Design view, board list, tldraw mounted, server-side board state and persistence, single user. Integration tests for board CRUD and snapshot persistence. 2. **Multiplayer:** diff sync and presence over ws. Tests boot the real server with two ws clients and assert diffs and cursors propagate and that presence stays out of chat.jsonl. 3. **Agents:** canvas HTTP API, prompt preamble, synthesized agent presence, design chat panel. Tests drive the API directly and assert ops broadcast and agent cursors emit. 4. **Polish:** cursor tweening, selection context in prompts, PNG export, theming pass, license decision. Two things to flag before implementation starts: the watermark question above, and the fact that this repo is live with other agents, so whoever implements should claim the `TopBar`/`App` seam in chat first to avoid collisions. Want me to start on phase 1? Sources: [tldraw agent starter kit](https://tldraw.dev/starter-kits/agent), [tldraw SDK license](https://tldraw.dev/legal/tldraw-license), [tldraw pricing](https://tldraw.dev/pricing), [tldraw AI docs](https://tldraw.dev/docs/ai)

step.text: Fixed. The inline attachment images were being blocked by the renderer's Content Security Policy, not by anything in the image pipeline. What was happening: `MessageImages` renders each attachment as an `` pointing at the session server, like `http://:/attachments/.png`. The CSP in `src/renderer/index.html` had `img-src 'self' data:`, so the browser blocked that request and the `` collapsed into the broken-icon-plus-filename pill you screenshotted. The link wrapping it opens the URL outside the page (where the CSP doesn't apply), which is why clicking showed the correct image. Uploads and fetches were never affected because `connect-src` already allowed `http:`. The fix is one line: `img-src` is now `'self' data: http:` in `src/renderer/index.html:8`, matching what `connect-src` already permits. This also covers images embedded in doc pages, since those get rewritten to the same http base. Verification: `yarn tsc --noEmit` passes. The full `yarn test` run had 3 failures in unrelated files (`agents`, `reconnect`, `providers` integration tests, all timeout-shaped), and all 3 pass when rerun in isolation, so that's the usual under-load flake, not this change. You'll need to restart the app (or let `yarn dev` reload) to pick up the new CSP.

files.diff:
+ import { docRefs, type DocPage } from '../../../shared/docs'
+ import type { PooledAgent } from '../../../shared/llm'
+ 
+ export type MentionToken =
+   | { kind: 'text'; text: string }
+   | { kind: 'agent'; text: string; agent: PooledAgent }
+   | { kind: 'doc'; text: string; page: string }
+ 
+ function escapeRegex(value: string): string {
+   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')
+ }
+ 
+ export function tokenizeMentions(
+   text: string,
+   agents: PooledAgent[],
+   docs: Record<string, DocPage>
+ ): MentionToken[] {
+   const refs = docRefs(docs)
+   const names = [...agents.map(a => `@${a.label}`), ...refs.map(ref => `#${ref.title}`)]
+     .sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)
+     .map(escapeRegex)
+   if (names.length === 0) return text ? [{ kind: 'text', text }] : []
+   const parts = text.split(new RegExp(`((?:${names.join('|')})(?![\\w-]))`, 'gi'))
+   const tokens: MentionToken[] = []
+   for (let index = 0; index < parts.length; index++) {
+     const part = parts[index]
+     if (!part) continue
+     if (index % 2 === 0) {
+       tokens.push({ kind: 'text', text: part })
+       continue
+     }
+     const name = part.slice(1).toLowerCase()
+     const agent = part.startsWith('@') ? agents.find(a => a.label.toLowerCase() === name) : undefined
+     const ref = part.startsWith('#') ? refs.find(r => r.title.toLowerCase() === name) : undefined
+     if (agent) tokens.push({ kind: 'agent', text: part, agent })
+     else if (ref) tokens.push({ kind: 'doc', text: part, page: ref.page })
+     else tokens.push({ kind: 'text', text: part })
+   }
+   return tokens
+ }
+

Done. The mention colors now show inside the composer input in both chat and threads.

What I changed:

- **Composer input highlighting** (`Composer.tsx`): the composer now draws a highlight layer under the textarea. The textarea's own text is transparent with a visible caret, and the layer renders the same text with agent mentions on the soft white background and doc mentions in baby blue on the faded blue background, exactly like they appear in messages. The layer scroll-syncs with the textarea and uses identical font metrics, so the caret and selection stay perfectly aligned while you type.
- **Doc pills in messages** (`ChatMessage.tsx`): the `DocMention` pill component existed from the earlier pass but nothing rendered it, so `#Doc Title` in a sent message showed as plain text. Message text now highlights both agent and doc mentions.
- **One shared tokenizer** (`mentionTokens.ts`, new): both places use the same parser, which matches the server's resolution rules from `mentionsIn` and `docMentionsIn` (case-insensitive, longest name wins, no match inside a longer word). So a mention only lights up if the server would actually resolve it, and the composer, the sent message, and the agent's doc context all agree.

+ import { create } from 'zustand'
+ 
+ export type BrowserTab = {
+   id: string
+   initialUrl: string
+   url: string
+   title: string
+   favicon: string | null
+   loading: boolean
+   canGoBack: boolean
+   canGoForward: boolean
+ }
+ 
+ type BrowserState = {
+   open: boolean
+   width: number
+   tabs: BrowserTab[]
+   activeTabId: string | null
+   openPanel(): void
+   closePanel(): void
+   setWidth(width: number): void
+   openUrl(url: string): void
+   addTab(): void
+   selectTab(id: string): void
+   closeTab(id: string): void
+   navigateTab(id: string, url: string): void
+   updateTab(id: string, patch: Partial<BrowserTab>): void
+ }
+ 
+ let seq = 0
+ 
+ function makeTab(url = ''): BrowserTab {
+   seq += 1
+   return {
+     id: `tab-${seq}`,
+     initialUrl: url,
+     url,
+     title: '',
+     favicon: null,
+     loading: false,
+     canGoBack: false,
+     canGoForward: false
+   }
+ }
+ 
+ function clampWidth(width: number): number {
+   const max = Math.max(360, window.innerWidth - 440)
+   return Math.min(Math.max(width, 360), max)
+ }
+ 
+ export const useBrowser = create<BrowserState>((set, get) => ({
+   open: false,
+   width: 480,
+   tabs: [],
+   activeTabId: null,
+   openPanel: () => {
+     if (get().tabs.length === 0) {
+       const tab = makeTab()
+       set({ open: true, tabs: [tab], activeTabId: tab.id })
+       return
+     }
+     set({ open: true })
+   },
+   closePanel: () => set({ open: false }),
+   setWidth: width => set({ width: clampWidth(width) }),
+   openUrl: url => {
+     const { tabs, activeTabId } = get()
+     const existing = tabs.find(t => t.url === url)
+     if (existing) {
+       set({ open: true, activeTabId: existing.id })
+       return
+     }
+     const active = tabs.find(t => t.id === activeTabId)
+     if (active && !active.initialUrl) {
+       set(s => ({
+         open: true,
+         tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === active.id ? { ...t, initialUrl: url, url } : t))
+       }))
+       return
+     }
+     const tab = makeTab(url)
+     set(s => ({ open: true, tabs: [...s.tabs, tab], activeTabId: tab.id }))
+   },
+   addTab: () => {
+     const tab = makeTab()
+     set(s => ({ tabs: [...s.tabs, tab], activeTabId: tab.id }))
+   },
+   selectTab: id => set({ activeTabId: id }),
+   closeTab: id =>
+     set(s => {
+       const index = s.tabs.findIndex(t => t.id === id)
+       const tabs = s.tabs.filter(t => t.id !== id)
+       const activeTabId =
+         s.activeTabId === id ? (tabs[Math.min(index, tabs.length - 1)]?.id ?? null) : s.activeTabId
+       return { tabs, activeTabId, open: tabs.length === 0 ? false : s.open }
+     }),
+   navigateTab: (id, url) =>
+     set(s => ({ tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === id ? { ...t, initialUrl: url, url } : t)) })),
+   updateTab: (id, patch) =>
+     set(s => ({ tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === id ? { ...t, ...patch } : t)) }))
+ }))
+

+ import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
+ import { useBrowser, type BrowserTab } from '../state/browser'
+ 
+ const views = new Map<string, WebviewElement>()
+ 
+ export function viewFor(id: string): WebviewElement | null {
+   return views.get(id) ?? null
+ }
+ 
+ export default function BrowserTabView({ tab, active }: { tab: BrowserTab; active: boolean }) {
+   const ref = useRef<WebviewElement>(null)
+ 
+   useEffect(() => {
+     const view = ref.current
+     if (!view) return
+     views.set(tab.id, view)
+     const update = useBrowser.getState().updateTab
+     const sync = () =>
+       update(tab.id, {
+         url: view.getURL(),
+         canGoBack: view.canGoBack(),
+         canGoForward: view.canGoForward()
+       })
+     const onTitle = (event: Event) => update(tab.id, { title: (event as Event & { title: string }).title })
+     const onFavicon = (event: Event) =>
+       update(tab.id, { favicon: (event as Event & { favicons: string[] }).favicons[0] ?? null })
+     const onStart = () => update(tab.id, { loading: true })
+     const onStop = () => {
+       update(tab.id, { loading: false })
+       sync()
+     }
+     view.addEventListener('did-navigate', sync)
+     view.addEventListener('did-navigate-in-page', sync)
+     view.addEventListener('page-title-updated', onTitle)
+     view.addEventListener('page-favicon-updated', onFavicon)
+     view.addEventListener('did-start-loading', onStart)
+     view.addEventListener('did-stop-loading', onStop)
+     return () => {
+       views.delete(tab.id)
+       view.removeEventListener('did-navigate', sync)
+       view.removeEventListener('did-navigate-in-page', sync)
+       view.removeEventListener('page-title-updated', onTitle)
+       view.removeEventListener('page-favicon-updated', onFavicon)
+       view.removeEventListener('did-start-loading', onStart)
+       view.removeEventListener('did-stop-loading', onStop)
+     }
+   }, [tab.id])
+ 
+   return (
+     <webview
+       ref={ref}
+       src={tab.initialUrl}
+       allowpopups="true"
+       className="absolute inset-0 w-full h-full"
+       style={{ visibility: active ? 'visible' : 'hidden' }}
+     />
+   )
+ }
+

+ export default function Markdown({ text }: { text: string }) {
+   const html = DOMPurify.sanitize(marked.parse(text, { async: false }) as string)
+ 
+   const onClick = (event: MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
+     const link = (event.target as HTMLElement).closest('a')
+     if (!link) return
+     event.preventDefault()
+     const href = link.getAttribute('href') ?? ''
+     if (/^https?:/i.test(href)) useBrowser.getState().openUrl(href)
+     else if (/^mailto:/i.test(href)) void window.crew.openExternal(href)
+   }
+ 
+   return <div className="md" onClick={onClick} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
+ }

+ import { docRefs, resolveDocRef, type DocMentionRef, type DocPage } from '../../../shared/docs'
+ import type { PooledAgent } from '../../../shared/llm'
+ 
+ export type MentionToken =
+   | { kind: 'text'; text: string }
+   | { kind: 'agent'; text: string; agent: PooledAgent }
+   | { kind: 'doc'; text: string; page: string | null }
+ 
+ function escapeRegex(value: string): string {
+   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')
+ }
+ 
+ export function tokenizeMentions(
+   text: string,
+   agents: PooledAgent[],
+   docs: Record<string, DocPage>,
+   docMentions?: DocMentionRef[]
+ ): MentionToken[] {
+   const refs = docMentions
+     ? docMentions
+         .filter(ref => ref.title.trim().length > 0)
+         .map(ref => ({ title: ref.title, page: resolveDocRef(docs, ref) }))
+     : docRefs(docs).map(ref => ({ title: ref.title, page: ref.page as string | null }))
+   const names = [...agents.map(a => `@${a.label}`), ...refs.map(ref => `#${ref.title}`)]
+     .sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)
+     .map(escapeRegex)
+   if (names.length === 0) return text ? [{ kind: 'text', text }] : []
+   const parts = text.split(new RegExp(`((?:${names.join('|')})(?![\\w-]))`, 'gi'))
+   const tokens: MentionToken[] = []
+   for (let index = 0; index < parts.length; index++) {
+     const part = parts[index]
+     if (!part) continue
+     if (index % 2 === 0) {
+       tokens.push({ kind: 'text', text: part })
+       continue
+     }
+     const name = part.slice(1).toLowerCase()
+     const agent = part.startsWith('@') ? agents.find(a => a.label.toLowerCase() === name) : undefined
+     const ref = part.startsWith('#') ? refs.find(r => r.title.toLowerCase() === name) : undefined
+     if (agent) tokens.push({ kind: 'agent', text: part, agent })
+     else if (ref) tokens.push({ kind: 'doc', text: part, page: ref.page })
+     else tokens.push({ kind: 'text', text: part })
+   }
+   return tokens
+ }
+

**Why it happened:** agent replies render markdown into plain `<a href>` tags, and nothing anywhere intercepted clicks or navigation, so a click loaded the URL into the app window itself.

**What I built:**

- **A Codex-style right panel.** Clicking a link in any agent message now pushes the chat to the left and opens the page in a browser panel beside it. It has pill-style page tabs (favicon, title, close on hover, plus button), back/forward/reload, an editable URL bar (plain text searches Google, bare domains get https), a spinner while loading, and an "open in your browser" button that hands the page to your real browser. The panel is resizable by dragging its left edge, and there's a globe toggle in the top bar next to Tasks. Closing the panel keeps your tabs alive for when you reopen it. The shell is set up so Files, terminal, and other views can slot in as future tabs.
- **App-wide navigation guards as the safety net.** The main process now blocks any navigation away from the app (`will-navigate` + window-open handlers) and reroutes those URLs into the panel instead, so even links outside chat markdown (like attachment previews) can't replace the app. Links opened from inside the panel's web pages, including target=_blank popups, navigate the panel tab rather than spawning windows.

New files are `state/browser.ts` (panel/tab store), `components/SidePanel.tsx`, `BrowserPanel.tsx`, and `BrowserTabView.tsx`, with small edits to `App.tsx`, `TopBar.tsx`, `Markdown.tsx`, `main.tsx`, `index.html` (CSP now allows https favicons), `preload.ts`, `env.d.ts`, and `src/main/index.ts` (webview enabled plus the guards and an `openExternal` bridge).

Verified with `yarn tsc --noEmit` clean, `yarn build` clean, and `yarn test` green (189 passed, 5 skipped). No new tests since the suite only covers server/runner behavior and there's no renderer harness; this one really needs eyes on it anyway, so give it a restart and click a link. One heads-up: mid-work the typecheck briefly failed on someone else's in-flight `session.ts` docMentions change, which resolved itself before my final run.

+ import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'
+ import {
+   DESIGN_COLORS,
+   richTextOf,
+   type DesignDocument,
+   type DesignOp,
+   type DesignOpResult,
+   type DesignShapeKind
+ } from '../shared/design'
+ 
+ const GEO_KINDS = new Set([
+   'rectangle',
+   'ellipse',
+   'triangle',
+   'diamond',
+   'star',
+   'cloud',
+   'hexagon',
+   'oval',
+   'x-box',
+   'check-box'
+ ])
+ 
+ const FILLS = new Set(['none', 'semi', 'solid', 'pattern'])
+ const COLORS = new Set<string>(DESIGN_COLORS)
+ const INDEX_DIGITS = '0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
+ 
+ interface ShapeRecord {
+   id: string
+   typeName: 'shape'
+   type: string
+   x: number
+   y: number
+   rotation: number
+   index: string
+   parentId: string
+   isLocked: boolean
+   opacity: number
+   meta: Record<string, never>
+   props: Record<string, unknown>
+ }
+ 
+ export interface AppliedOps {
+   put: ShapeRecord[]
+   remove: string[]
+   results: DesignOpResult[]
+   cursors: Array<{ x: number; y: number }>
+ }
+ 
+ export function newShapeId(): string {
+   return `shape:${randomBytes(8).toString('hex')}`
+ }
+ 
+ // Fractional index keys sort as plain strings. Bumping the last digit (or
+ // appending when it is already the largest) always yields a valid key that
+ // sorts above everything present, which is all stacking order needs here.
+ export function indexAbove(top: string | null): string {
+   if (!top) return 'a1'
+   const last = top[top.length - 1]
+   const at = INDEX_DIGITS.indexOf(last)
+   if (at === -1 || last === 'z') return `${top}1`
+   return top.slice(0, -1) + INDEX_DIGITS[at + 1]
+ }
+ 
+ function pageIdOf(document: DesignDocument): string | null {
+   for (const [id] of Object.entries(document.store)) {
+     if (id.startsWith('page:')) return id
+   }
+   return null
+ }
+ 
+ function topIndexOn(document: DesignDocument, parentId: string): string | null {
+   let top: string | null = null
+   for (const record of Object.values(document.store)) {
+     const shape = record as Partial<ShapeRecord>
+     if (shape.typeName !== 'shape' || shape.parentId !== parentId) continue
+     if (typeof shape.index === 'string' && (top === null || shape.index > top)) top = shape.index
+   }
+   return top
+ }
+ 
+ function baseProps(color: string, fill: string, text: string): Record<string, unknown> {
+   return {
+     dash: 'draw',
+     url: '',
+     growY: 0,
+     scale: 1,
+     labelColor: 'black',
+     color,
+     fill,
+     size: 'm',
+     font: 'draw',
+     align: 'middle',
+     verticalAlign: 'middle',
+     richText: richTextOf(text)
+   }
+ }
+ 
+ function propsFor(kind: DesignShapeKind, op: Extract<DesignOp, { op: 'create' }>): Record<string, unknown> {
+   const color = op.color && COLORS.has(op.color) ? op.color : 'black'
+   const fill = op.fill && FILLS.has(op.fill) ? op.fill : 'none'
+   const text = op.text ?? ''
+   const w = op.w && op.w > 0 ? op.w : 200
+   const h = op.h && op.h > 0 ? op.h : kind === 'frame' ? 200 : 120
+   if (GEO_KINDS.has(kind)) return { ...baseProps(color, fill, text), geo: kind, w, h }
+   switch (kind) {
+     case 'text':
+       return {
+         color,
+         size: 'm',
+         font: 'draw',
+         textAlign: 'start',
+         w: op.w && op.w > 0 ? op.w : 300,
+         richText: richTextOf(text),
+         scale: 1,
+         autoSize: op.w === undefined
+       }
+     case 'note':
+       return {
+         color: op.color && COLORS.has(op.color) ? op.color : 'yellow',
+         labelColor: 'black',
+         size: 'm',
+         font: 'draw',
+         fontSizeAdjustment: null,
+         align: 'middle',
+         verticalAlign: 'middle',
+         growY: 0,
+         url: '',
+         richText: richTextOf(text),
+         scale: 1,
+         textLastEditedBy: null
+       }
+     case 'frame':
+       return { w, h, name: op.name ?? op.text ?? 'Frame', color: 'black' }
+     case 'arrow':
+       return {
+         kind: 'arc',
+         labelColor: 'black',
+         color,
+         fill,
+         dash: 'draw',
+         size: 'm',
+         arrowheadStart: 'none',
+         arrowheadEnd: 'arrow',
+         font: 'draw',
+         start: { x: 0, y: 0 },
+         end: { x: (op.endX ?? op.x + 200) - op.x, y: (op.endY ?? op.y) - op.y },
+         bend: 0,
+         richText: richTextOf(text),
+         labelPosition: 0.5,
+         scale: 1,
+         elbowMidPoint: 0.5
+       }
+     case 'line':
+       return {
+         color,
+         dash: 'draw',
+         size: 'm',
+         spline: 'line',
+         points: {
+           a1: { id: 'a1', index: 'a1', x: 0, y: 0 },
+           a2: { id: 'a2', index: 'a2', x: (op.endX ?? op.x + 200) - op.x, y: (op.endY ?? op.y) - op.y }
+         },
+         scale: 1
+       }
+     default:
+       return {}
+   }
+ }
+ 
+ const SHAPE_TYPE: Record<string, string> = {
+   text: 'text',
+   note: 'note',
+   frame: 'frame',
+   arrow: 'arrow',
+   line: 'line'
+ }
+ 
+ function typeFor(kind: DesignShapeKind): string | null {
+   if (GEO_KINDS.has(kind)) return 'geo'
+   return SHAPE_TYPE[kind] ?? null
+ }
+ 
+ function shapeAt(document: DesignDocument, id: string): ShapeRecord | null {
+   const record = document.store[id] as ShapeRecord | undefined
+   return record && record.typeName === 'shape' ? record : null
+ }
+ 
+ function childrenOf(document: DesignDocument, id: string): string[] {
+   const out: string[] = []
+   for (const [recordId, record] of Object.entries(document.store)) {
+     const shape = record as Partial<ShapeRecord>
+     if (shape.typeName === 'shape' && shape.parentId === id) {
+       out.push(recordId, ...childrenOf(document, recordId))
+     }
+   }
+   return out
+ }
+ 
+ function applyCreate(document: DesignDocument, op: Extract<DesignOp, { op: 'create' }>, applied: AppliedOps): void {
+   const type = typeFor(op.kind)
+   if (!type) {
+     applied.results.push({ error: `Unknown shape kind: ${String(op.kind)}` })
+     return
+   }
+   if (typeof op.x !== 'number' || typeof op.y !== 'number' || !isFinite(op.x) || !isFinite(op.y)) {
+     applied.results.push({ error: 'x and y must be numbers' })
+     return
+   }
+   const parentId = op.parent && shapeAt(document, op.parent)?.type === 'frame' ? op.parent : pageIdOf(document)
+   if (!parentId) {
+     applied.results.push({ error: 'Board has no page yet. Open it in the app first.' })
+     return
+   }
+   const record: ShapeRecord = {
+     id: newShapeId(),
+     typeName: 'shape',
+     type,
+     x: op.x,
+     y: op.y,
+     rotation: 0,
+     index: indexAbove(topIndexOn(document, parentId)),
+     parentId,
+     isLocked: false,
+     opacity: 1,
+     meta: {},
+     props: propsFor(op.kind, op)
+   }
+   document.store[record.id] = record
+   applied.put.push(record)
+   applied.results.push({ id: record.id })
+   applied.cursors.push({ x: op.x, y: op.y })
+ }
+ 
+ function applyUpdate(document: DesignDocument, op: Extract<DesignOp, { op: 'update' }>, applied: AppliedOps): void {
+   const shape = shapeAt(document, op.id)
+   if (!shape) {
+     applied.results.push({ error: `No shape ${op.id}` })
+     return
+   }
+   const next: ShapeRecord = { ...shape, props: { ...shape.props } }
+   if (typeof op.x === 'number' && isFinite(op.x)) next.x = op.x
+   if (typeof op.y === 'number' && isFinite(op.y)) next.y = op.y
+   if (typeof op.w === 'number' && op.w > 0 && 'w' in next.props) next.props.w = op.w
+   if (typeof op.h === 'number' && op.h > 0 && 'h' in next.props) next.props.h = op.h
+   if (typeof op.text === 'string' && 'richText' in next.props) next.props.richText = richTextOf(op.text)
+   if (op.color && COLORS.has(op.color) && 'color' in next.props) next.props.color = op.color
+   if (op.fill && FILLS.has(op.fill) && 'fill' in next.props) next.props.fill = op.fill
+   if (typeof op.name === 'string' && shape.type === 'frame') next.props.name = op.name
+   document.store[op.id] = next
+   applied.put.push(next)
+   applied.results.push({ id: op.id })
+   applied.cursors.push({ x: next.x, y: next.y })
+ }
+ 
+ function applyDelete(document: DesignDocument, op: Extract<DesignOp, { op: 'delete' }>, applied: AppliedOps): void {
+   const shape = shapeAt(document, op.id)
+   if (!shape) {
+     applied.results.push({ error: `No shape ${op.id}` })
+     return
+   }
+   applied.cursors.push({ x: shape.x, y: shape.y })
+   for (const id of [op.id, ...childrenOf(document, op.id)]) {
+     delete document.store[id]
+     applied.remove.push(id)
+   }
+   applied.results.push({ id: op.id })
+ }
+ 
+ export function applyDesignOps(document: DesignDocument, ops: DesignOp[]): AppliedOps {
+   const applied: AppliedOps = { put: [], remove: [], results: [], cursors: [] }
+   for (const op of ops) {
+     if (!op || typeof op !== 'object') {
+       applied.results.push({ error: 'Not an op' })
+       continue
+     }
+     if (op.op === 'create') applyCreate(document, op, applied)
+     else if (op.op === 'update') applyUpdate(document, op, applied)
+     else if (op.op === 'delete') applyDelete(document, op, applied)
+     else if (op.op === 'point' && typeof op.x === 'number' && typeof op.y === 'number') {
+       applied.results.push({})
+       applied.cursors.push({ x: op.x, y: op.y })
+     } else applied.results.push({ error: `Unknown op: ${String((op as { op?: unknown }).op)}` })
+   }
+   return applied
+ }
+ 
+ export function boardSummary(id: string, name: string, document: DesignDocument | null): unknown {
+   const shapes: unknown[] = []
+   if (document) {
+     for (const record of Object.values(document.store)) {
+       const shape = record as Partial<ShapeRecord>
+       if (shape.typeName !== 'shape') continue
+       const props = (shape.props ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>
+       shapes.push({
+         id: shape.id,
+         kind: shape.type === 'geo' ? props.geo : shape.type,
+         x: shape.x,
+         y: shape.y,
+         w: props.w,
+         h: props.h,
+         text:
+           shape.type === 'frame'
+             ? props.name
+             : 'richText' in props
+               ? plainText(props.richText)
+               : undefined,
+         color: props.color,
+         fill: props.fill,
+         parentId: shape.parentId?.startsWith('shape:') ? shape.parentId : undefined
+       })
+     }
+   }
+   return { id, name, shapes }
+ }
+ 
+ function plainText(richText: unknown): string {
+   const doc = richText as { content?: Array<{ content?: Array<{ text?: string }> }> } | undefined
+   if (!doc?.content) return ''
+   return doc.content.map(p => (p.content ?? []).map(s => s.text ?? '').join('')).join('\n')
+ }
+

Your other two pages (`this-is-a-parent-page`, `this-is-a-child-page`) were created before codes existed, which is why you don't see ids on them.
