The shortcode is good enough, and I tightened one edge I found while checking. Here's the math:

**Collision odds.** A code is a digit followed by 3 letters or digits, so there are about 457,000 possible codes. But collisions mostly can't happen by chance: when a page is created, the generator checks every existing page's code and rerolls until it finds a free one. On a single machine a duplicate is impossible. The only true window is two people creating pages at the same moment on different machines, before git sync catches up. For that to collide, both machines must roll the identical code: about 1 in 457,000, or 0.0002% per simultaneous pair. Even if it ever happened, the damage is small: a reference would show the wrong page's hover card until one of the two pages is renamed. No data is lost.

**Should it be longer?** No. Length matters when the code space gets crowded, and a crew docs tree measured in hundreds of pages uses under 0.1% of the space. A 5th character would multiply the space by 36 but make every filename uglier for no practical gain. If it ever needs to grow, it's a small change since the code is just a filename suffix.

**The edge I fixed.** The old pattern would misread a plain year as a code: a legacy page named `report-2024.md` would be treated as already having id `2024`, skipped by the migration, and it would collide with any other page ending in the same year. Codes now must contain at least one letter, which a year never does, so `report-2024` correctly gets a fresh code appended at startup. Your existing page (`1ydl`) has a letter and is unaffected. Added test coverage for exactly this case.

**One heads-up not related to my change:** the current synced `session.ts` calls board methods (`boardList`, `handleDesignCreate`, etc.) that don't exist in the committed code, so someone's design-boards work is half-landed. It fails typecheck and crashes every client join in tests, which is why 2 of my 7 doc-mention tests (the ones that connect a UI) time out at HEAD. The 5 that don't join a client all pass, including the new migration case, and the two failures die in `handleHello` before any doc code runs. Whoever is on boards should sync the other half.

+   private runPrompt(
+     promptId: string,
+     forAgentId: string,
+     threadId: string,
+     text: string,
+     settings: AgentSettings,
+     attachments: Attachment[],
+     designBoard?: DesignBoardMeta
+   ): void {
+     const agent = this.agents.get(forAgentId)
+     if (!agent) {
+       this.send({ type: 'agent.error', promptId, message: 'That agent is not on this machine.' })
+       return
+     }
+     if (this.accepted.has(promptId)) return
+     this.accepted.add(promptId)
+     // The design preamble is written here rather than on the host because only
+     // this side knows the http address it reaches the server at.
+     const body = designBoard ? `${text}\n\n${designPreamble(this.httpBase, designBoard, forAgentId)}` : text
+     const tail = this.tails.get(threadId) ?? Promise.resolve()
+     const next = tail
+       .then(() => this.execute(agent.provider, promptId, body, settings, attachments))
+       .catch(() => {})

+ ---
+ name: crew-design-tab
+ description: Design tab (tldraw canvas) architecture decisions, the Vite optimizeDeps gotcha, and the open watermark/license question
+ metadata:
+   type: project
+ ---
+ 
+ The Design tab (built 2026-07-23) is a tldraw 5.x canvas synced over crew's own ws protocol. Key decisions, not obvious from the code:
+ 
+ - Sync is server-authoritative, record-level last-writer-wins. No CRDT. The first client to open an empty board sends `design.init` with its store snapshot; the server never builds tldraw documents itself.
+ - Agents edit boards through `GET/POST /design/:id(/ops)` on the host HTTP server with a simple op JSON (curl from the CLI). The op-to-record templates live in `src/server/designops.ts` and are validated against the real tldraw schema in `tests/design-api.integration.test.ts`. If tldraw is upgraded, that test is what catches shape prop drift.
+ - Agent cursors are synthesized server-side from applied ops (140ms steps), rendered as pet-icon DOM overlays with CSS transitions. Human cursors use tldraw's native instance_presence records. tldraw 5 renders native cursors on a canvas overlay, so pet cursors could not use a component override.
+ - `@tldraw/assets` must stay in `optimizeDeps.exclude` in electron.vite.config.ts. Vite's dep pre-bundler drops the `?url` import suffix and `getAssetUrlsByImport()` crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')" in dev. Changing that config needs a `yarn dev` restart.
+ - Open decision: the free tldraw license shows a "made with tldraw" watermark. Removing it needs a paid business license. Jamel deferred this.
+ 
+ Related: [[crew-agents-threads]], [[crew-design-system]]
+

+ import { create } from 'zustand'
+ 
+ export type BrowserTab = {
+   id: string
+   kind: 'web' | 'file'
+   initialUrl: string
+   url: string
+   title: string
+   favicon: string | null
+   loading: boolean
+   canGoBack: boolean
+   canGoForward: boolean
+   path: string
+   line: number | null
+   back: string[]
+   forward: string[]
+   generation: number
+ }
+ 
+ type BrowserState = {
+   width: number
+   tabs: BrowserTab[]
+   activeTabId: string | null
+   setWidth(width: number): void
+   openUrl(url: string): void
+   openFile(path: string, line?: number | null): void
+   addTab(): void
+   selectTab(id: string): void
+   closeTab(id: string): void
+   closeAll(): void
+   navigateTab(id: string, url: string): void
+   navigateFile(id: string, path: string): void
+   fileBack(id: string): void
+   fileForward(id: string): void
+   reloadFile(id: string): void
+   updateTab(id: string, patch: Partial<BrowserTab>): void
+ }
+ 
+ let seq = 0
+ 
+ function makeTab(url = ''): BrowserTab {
+   seq += 1
+   return {
+     id: `tab-${seq}`,
+     kind: 'web',
+     initialUrl: url,
+     url,
+     title: '',
+     favicon: null,
+     loading: false,
+     canGoBack: false,
+     canGoForward: false,
+     path: '',
+     line: null,
+     back: [],
+     forward: [],
+     generation: 0
+   }
+ }
+ 
+ function clampWidth(width: number): number {
+   const max = Math.max(360, window.innerWidth - 440)
+   return Math.min(Math.max(width, 360), max)
+ }
+ 
+ export const useBrowser = create<BrowserState>((set, get) => ({
+   width: 480,
+   tabs: [],
+   activeTabId: null,
+   setWidth: width => set({ width: clampWidth(width) }),
+   openUrl: url => {
+     const { tabs, activeTabId } = get()
+     const existing = tabs.find(t => t.kind === 'web' && t.url === url)
+     if (existing) {
+       set({ activeTabId: existing.id })
+       return
+     }
+     const active = tabs.find(t => t.id === activeTabId)
+     if (active && active.kind === 'web' && !active.initialUrl) {
+       set(s => ({
+         tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === active.id ? { ...t, initialUrl: url, url } : t))
+       }))
+       return
+     }
+     const tab = makeTab(url)
+     set(s => ({ tabs: [...s.tabs, tab], activeTabId: tab.id }))
+   },
+   openFile: (path, line = null) => {
+     const { tabs, activeTabId } = get()
+     const existing = tabs.find(t => t.kind === 'file' && t.path === path)
+     if (existing) {
+       set(s => ({
+         activeTabId: existing.id,
+         tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === existing.id ? { ...t, line } : t))
+       }))
+       return
+     }
+     const active = tabs.find(t => t.id === activeTabId)
+     if (active && active.kind === 'web' && !active.initialUrl) {
+       set(s => ({
+         tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === active.id ? { ...t, kind: 'file' as const, path, line } : t))
+       }))
+       return
+     }
+     const tab = { ...makeTab(), kind: 'file' as const, path, line }
+     set(s => ({ tabs: [...s.tabs, tab], activeTabId: tab.id }))
+   },
+   addTab: () => {
+     const tab = makeTab()
+     set(s => ({ tabs: [...s.tabs, tab], activeTabId: tab.id }))
+   },
+   selectTab: id => set({ activeTabId: id }),
+   closeTab: id =>
+     set(s => {
+       const index = s.tabs.findIndex(t => t.id === id)
+       const tabs = s.tabs.filter(t => t.id !== id)
+       const activeTabId =
+         s.activeTabId === id ? (tabs[Math.min(index, tabs.length - 1)]?.id ?? null) : s.activeTabId
+       return { tabs, activeTabId }
+     }),
+   closeAll: () => set({ tabs: [], activeTabId: null }),
+   navigateTab: (id, url) =>
+     set(s => ({ tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === id ? { ...t, initialUrl: url, url } : t)) })),
+   navigateFile: (id, path) =>
+     set(s => ({
+       tabs: s.tabs.map(t =>
+         t.id === id && t.path !== path
+           ? { ...t, path, line: null, back: [...t.back, t.path], forward: [] }
+           : t
+       )
+     })),
+   fileBack: id =>
+     set(s => ({
+       tabs: s.tabs.map(t => {
+         if (t.id !== id || t.back.length === 0) return t
+         const path = t.back[t.back.length - 1]
+         return { ...t, path, line: null, back: t.back.slice(0, -1), forward: [t.path, ...t.forward] }
+       })
+     })),
+   fileForward: id =>
+     set(s => ({
+       tabs: s.tabs.map(t => {
+         if (t.id !== id || t.forward.length === 0) return t
+         const path = t.forward[0]
+         return { ...t, path, line: null, back: [...t.back, t.path], forward: t.forward.slice(1) }
+       })
+     })),
+   reloadFile: id =>
+     set(s => ({ tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === id ? { ...t, generation: t.generation + 1 } : t)) })),
+   updateTab: (id, patch) =>
+     set(s => ({ tabs: s.tabs.map(t => (t.id === id ? { ...t, ...patch } : t)) }))
+ }))
+

+ import DOMPurify from 'dompurify'
+ import { marked } from 'marked'
+ import { useMemo, type MouseEvent } from 'react'
+ import { useBrowser } from '../state/browser'
+ import { linkifyFiles, parseFileRef } from './fileLinks'
+ 
+ export default function Markdown({ text }: { text: string }) {
+   const html = useMemo(() => {
+     const container = document.createElement('div')
+     container.innerHTML = DOMPurify.sanitize(marked.parse(text, { async: false }) as string)
+     linkifyFiles(container)
+     return container.innerHTML
+   }, [text])
+ 
+   const onClick = (event: MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
+     const link = (event.target as HTMLElement).closest('a')
+     if (!link) return
+     event.preventDefault()
+     if (link.dataset.path !== undefined) {
+       const line = link.dataset.line ? parseInt(link.dataset.line, 10) : null
+       useBrowser.getState().openFile(link.dataset.path, line)
+       return
+     }
+     const href = link.getAttribute('href') ?? ''
+     if (/^https?:/i.test(href)) {
+       useBrowser.getState().openUrl(href)
+       return
+     }
+     if (/^mailto:/i.test(href)) {
+       void window.crew.openExternal(href)
+       return
+     }
+     const ref = parseFileRef(decodeURIComponent(href))
+     if (ref) useBrowser.getState().openFile(ref.path, ref.line)
+   }
+ 
+   return <div className="md" onClick={onClick} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
+ }

+ import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
+ import path from 'node:path'
+ import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+ import { readRepoFile, resolveRepoPath } from '../src/main/files'
+ import { tmpDir } from './helpers/session'
+ 
+ function makeRepo(): string {
+   const root = tmpDir('files')
+   mkdirSync(path.join(root, '.git'))
+   mkdirSync(path.join(root, 'src', 'app'), { recursive: true })
+   writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'readme.md'), 'hello\nworld\n')
+   writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'src', 'app', 'main.ts'), 'export const x = 1\n')
+   writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'logo.png'), Buffer.from([0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x00, 0x01]))
+   return root
+ }
+ 
+ describe('readRepoFile', () => {
+   it('reads a text file with a normalized path', async () => {
+     const root = makeRepo()
+     const result = await readRepoFile(root, './readme.md')
+     expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'file', path: 'readme.md', text: 'hello\nworld\n', truncated: false })
+   })
+ 
+   it('lists the root with folders first and hides .git', async () => {
+     const root = makeRepo()
+     const result = await readRepoFile(root, '')
+     expect(result.kind).toBe('dir')
+     if (result.kind !== 'dir') return
+     expect(result.path).toBe('')
+     expect(result.entries).toEqual([
+       { name: 'src', dir: true },
+       { name: 'logo.png', dir: false },
+       { name: 'readme.md', dir: false }
+     ])
+   })
+ 
+   it('lists a nested folder', async () => {
+     const root = makeRepo()
+     const result = await readRepoFile(root, 'src/app/')
+     expect(result.kind).toBe('dir')
+     if (result.kind !== 'dir') return
+     expect(result.path).toBe('src/app')
+     expect(result.entries).toEqual([{ name: 'main.ts', dir: false }])
+   })
+ 
+   it('reports a missing file', async () => {
+     const root = makeRepo()
+     const result = await readRepoFile(root, 'src/gone.ts')
+     expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'missing', path: 'src/gone.ts' })
+   })
+ 
+   it('refuses paths that escape the folder', async () => {
+     const root = makeRepo()
+     const result = await readRepoFile(root, '../outside.txt')
+     expect(result.kind).toBe('missing')
+     expect(resolveRepoPath(root, '../outside.txt')).toBeNull()
+     expect(resolveRepoPath(root, 'src/../../outside.txt')).toBeNull()
+   })
+ 
+   it('marks binary files instead of returning garbage', async () => {
+     const root = makeRepo()
+     const result = await readRepoFile(root, 'logo.png')
+     expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'binary', path: 'logo.png', size: 6 })
+   })
+ 
+   it('truncates very large files', async () => {
+     const root = makeRepo()
+     writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'big.txt'), 'a'.repeat(600 * 1024))
+     const result = await readRepoFile(root, 'big.txt')
+     expect(result.kind).toBe('file')
+     if (result.kind !== 'file') return
+     expect(result.truncated).toBe(true)
+     expect(result.text.length).toBe(512 * 1024)
+   })
+ })

step.text:
Done and green: 222 tests pass plus the 16 new ones, and `tsc --noEmit` is clean. The browser panel now doubles as a Codex-style file browser, and file mentions across chat and threads are links that open it.

**What clicking a file does now**

Any file reference opens a file tab in the side panel, alongside web tabs. A file tab shows the Codex-style viewer: a breadcrumb path bar (each segment clickable, with a root folder icon), line numbers in a gutter, and when the link carried a line number (`src/app.ts:12`) that line is highlighted and scrolled into view. Opening a folder shows its listing, folders first, and you can drill down or climb the breadcrumbs. File tabs get their own back/forward history, a reload button, and a "Show in folder" button that reveals the file in Finder. Missing files, binary files, and files over 512 KB get friendly states instead of garbage.

**Where file links appear**

- Agent replies (markdown): backticked paths like `` `src/app.ts:12` ``, bare paths in prose, and relative markdown links all become clickable chips. URLs, version numbers like `0.51.4`, and domains are left alone.
- Human messages: plain-text paths render as clickable chips next to the existing @agent and #doc mentions.
- Step rows and the "files changed" card: every path is clickable.

**How it works**

- `src/main/files.ts` reads files and folders strictly inside the session folder (path escapes resolve to "missing"), with binary sniffing and a size cap. Exposed through `AppSession` so it stays electron-free and testable, wired up as `file:read` / `file:reveal` IPC and `window.crew.readFile` / `revealFile`.
- `src/renderer/src/state/browser.ts` tabs now have a `web` or `file` kind, with `openFile`, per-tab history, and breadcrumb navigation.
- `src/renderer/src/components/fileLinks.tsx` holds the path detection (shared by markdown, plain text, and href parsing), and `FileView.tsx` is the viewer.

**Tests**: `tests/file-read.test.ts` covers the reader (normalization, dir listing order, .git hidden, escapes, binary, truncation); `tests/file-links-probe.test.ts` renders Markdown and BrowserPanel in jsdom and covers linkification rules, click-to-open with line targeting, breadcrumb browsing, and the missing-file state.

One judgment call: there's no syntax highlighting in the viewer, since the app has no highlighter dependency and diffs render plain today. If you want it, shiki would be the add.

+   rust: () => import('@shikijs/langs/rust'),

+   java: () => import('@shikijs/langs/java'),

+   swift: () => import('@shikijs/langs/swift'),
+   kotlin: () => import('@shikijs/langs/kotlin'),
+   sql: () => import('@shikijs/langs/sql'),
+   xml: () => import('@shikijs/langs/xml'),
+   diff: () => import('@shikijs/langs/diff'),
+   docker: () => import('@shikijs/langs/docker'),
+   make: () => import('@shikijs/langs/make')
+ }
+ 
+ const extensions: Record<string, string> = {
+   ts: 'typescript',
+   mts: 'typescript',
+   cts: 'typescript',
+   tsx: 'tsx',
+   js: 'javascript',
+   mjs: 'javascript',
+   cjs: 'javascript',
+   jsx: 'jsx',
+   json: 'json',
+   css: 'css',
+   html: 'html',
+   htm: 'html',
+   md: 'markdown',

+   yml: 'yaml',
+   yaml: 'yaml',
+   toml: 'toml',
+   sh: 'shellscript',
+   bash: 'shellscript',
+   zsh: 'shellscript',
+   py: 'python',
+   rs: 'rust',
+   go: 'go',
+   java: 'java',
+   c: 'c',
+   h: 'c',
+   cpp: 'cpp',
+   cc: 'cpp',
+   hpp: 'cpp',
+   rb: 'ruby',
+   php: 'php',
+   swift: 'swift',
+   kt: 'kotlin',
+   sql: 'sql',
+   xml: 'xml',
+   svg: 'xml',
+   diff: 'diff',
+   patch: 'diff'
+ }
+ 
+ const filenames: Record<string, string> = {
+   dockerfile: 'docker',
+   makefile: 'make'
+ }
+ 
+ export function languageFor(path: string): string | null {
+   const name = (path.split('/').pop() ?? '').toLowerCase()
+   const byName = filenames[name]
+   if (byName) return byName
+   const ext = name.includes('.') ? (name.split('.').pop() ?? '') : ''
+   return extensions[ext] ?? null
+ }
+ 
+ let corePromise: Promise<HighlighterCore> | null = null
+ const loading = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()
+ 
+ function core(): Promise<HighlighterCore> {
+   corePromise ??= createHighlighterCore({
+     themes: [import('@shikijs/themes/github-dark-default'), import('@shikijs/themes/github-light-default')],
+     langs: [],
+     engine: createJavaScriptRegexEngine({ forgiving: true })
+   })
+   return corePromise
+ }
+ 
+ async function withLanguage(lang: string): Promise<HighlighterCore> {
+   const highlighter = await core()
+   if (!highlighter.getLoadedLanguages().includes(lang)) {
+     let pending = loading.get(lang)
+     if (!pending) {
+       pending = highlighter.loadLanguage(languages[lang])
+       loading.set(lang, pending)
+     }
+     await pending
+   }
+   return highlighter
+ }
+ 
+ export async function highlightLines(
+   path: string,
+   text: string,
+   theme: Theme
+ ): Promise<ThemedToken[][] | null> {
+   const lang = languageFor(path)
+   if (!lang || text.length > MAX_CHARS) return null
+   try {
+     const highlighter = await withLanguage(lang)
+     return highlighter.codeToTokensBase(text, { lang, theme: themeNames[theme] })
+   } catch {
+     return null
+   }
+ }
+

Both are in, tested, and already synced by the app. `tsc --noEmit` is clean and the full suite passes (230 tests, including 12 new ones covering both features).

**Syntax highlighting**

The viewer now colors code with shiki, using its pure JavaScript engine, so no wasm and it runs fine in the jsdom tests. Grammars load lazily per language the first time you open a file of that type, with 26 languages mapped from extensions (TypeScript, TSX, Python, Rust, Go, CSS, YAML, shell, SQL, Dockerfile, Makefile, and so on). Unknown extensions just render plain like before. It follows the app theme: github-dark on dark, github-light in light mode, both on the app's own background. Files render instantly in plain text and the colors swap in when the grammar is ready, and very large files (over 200k characters) skip highlighting so the pane never stalls.

**Editing**

It turned out to be reasonable, so it's in. Text files get a small floating pencil button in the top corner of the viewer. Clicking it swaps the code view for a plain mono textarea holding the file, with Cancel and a white Save pill floating above. Cmd+S saves, Escape cancels, and Tab inserts spaces instead of jumping focus. Save writes through a new `file:write` IPC, and the viewer re-renders with the freshly highlighted result. Since the app auto-commits and pushes, saves ride the normal crew sync.

The write path has the same guardrails as reading: it only touches paths inside the session folder, only overwrites files that already exist (no creating files from the viewer), and refuses truncated-view files, so you can never blind-overwrite a 600 KB file with the 512 KB slice you were shown. Binary files and folders don't get the edit button at all.

One honest limitation: the editor itself is plain text, no colors while typing. Highlighted editing means pulling in CodeMirror, which felt like too much for this. If editing gets real use I can add it later.

Side note: `yarn add shiki` initially wiped electron from node_modules because your shell's `NODE_ENV=production` makes yarn skip devDependencies. A `NODE_ENV=development yarn install` fixed it, and I've noted the gotcha for next time.

+     if (unknown.length === 0) return

step.text:
Both things are done, tested, and already synced by the app. You now edit right in the highlighted view, and the linkifier no longer turns prose like "Undo/redo" into file links.

**Why there was a separate flow, and what changed**

The honest reason: a browser textarea can only display plain uncolored text, so the quick version swapped between a colored view and a plain editor. The fix is the standard trick real in-browser editors use, and the crew composer already uses it for mention highlighting: a textarea with invisible text sits exactly on top of the highlighted code, so you see the colored code and line numbers while your keystrokes, caret, and selection live in the textarea. The two layers share the same font metrics and padding, so they align to the pixel.

So now there's no edit mode at all. Click anywhere in a file and type. Line numbers update live as you add or remove lines, colors re-render as you type (with a tiny debounce so big files don't churn), and the gutter, target-line highlight, and breadcrumbs all stay put. Tab inserts spaces, Escape discards your changes, Cmd+S saves.

Saving stays explicit on purpose: every save auto-commits and pushes to everyone in the session, so keystrokes should not hit git as you type. The moment the file differs from disk, Discard and a white Save pill float in the corner. Save, and they disappear. Truncated and binary files stay read-only.

**The Undo/redo bug**

Regex tweaks would always leak (either/or, read/write, and so on), so I did what Codex does: a path only becomes a link if it actually exists in the project. There's a new lightweight `file:stat` IPC, and the renderer keeps a small cache of confirmed paths. Real paths get linked within a frame or two of rendering; prose with slashes stays plain text. Misses are re-checked after 15 seconds, so a file an agent just created starts linking shortly after it lands on disk. Explicit markdown links like `[app](src/app.ts)` are left alone since those are deliberate.

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean, and the full suite is green at 235 passing (43 files). That includes reworked coverage: in-place editing with save/discard/Cmd+S, colors persisting while typing, truncated files staying read-only, `statRepoFile` behavior, and a regression test that "Undo/redo moved" renders as plain text while a real path beside it still links. One unrelated runner CLI test flaked in a loaded full run and passes in isolation, which matches the suite's known behavior. Changes are already committed and pushed via crew sync.

One caveat worth knowing: with the overlay approach, typing many new lines at the bottom edge of the panel can let the caret walk out of view, since the outer pane, not the textarea, owns scrolling. I nudge the pane to follow the caret's line on each edit, which covers normal editing. If you ever want full editor behavior (multi-cursor, undo stacks, search), that's the point where CodeMirror earns its weight.

step.text:
I have the full picture now. Let me give you the honest read before I show code, because the answer to "how do we make it like that" turns on one thing.

**The blocker: tldraw's default shapes are the ceiling.**

Right now every shape on the board is a tldraw built-in (`geo`, `text`, `note`, `frame`, `arrow`, `line`). Those shapes have no corner radius, no fill/stroke separation, no arbitrary hex color (just 13 named ones), no auto layout, no components, no masks, no boolean ops, and no effects. That is also exactly why the agents produce flat squares: the op vocabulary in `src/shared/design.ts:58` literally only offers them a shape kind, a position, one of 13 colors, and one of 4 fills. An agent with good taste still cannot make anything good with that vocabulary. The problem is not the prompt, it's the material.

So no amount of toolbar buttons gets us there. We need our own node type. Here's the plan I'm building against:

**Keep tldraw as the engine, replace the shapes.** We keep camera, selection, snapping, undo, hit testing, and critically the whole git-synced store and presence layer we already have. We add one custom shape, `design-node`, rendered as real HTML instead of SVG. That last part is the unlock: HTML gives us `border-radius`, `backdrop-filter` (that's liquid glass, for free), `box-shadow`, real font stacks, and flexbox (that's auto layout, for free). Figma-grade visuals without writing a rasterizer.

Let me build the model.

+   name: string

+ export const SLASH_COMMANDS: SlashCommand[] = [
+   { name: 'plan', hint: 'Get a plan first, then implement it' }
+ ]
+ 
+ const PLAN_TOKEN = /(?:^|\s)\/plan(?=\s|$)/i
+ 
+ // '/plan' can sit anywhere in the line, so '@name /plan tidy the readme' and
+ // '/plan @name tidy the readme' both read the same way.
+ export function readPlanCommand(text: string): { planning: boolean; text: string } {
+   const match = PLAN_TOKEN.exec(text)
+   if (!match) return { planning: false, text }
+   const cut = text.slice(0, match.index) + text.slice(match.index + match[0].length)
+   return { planning: true, text: cut.trim() }
+ }
+ 
+ export function slashCandidates(value: string): SlashCommand[] {
+   const match = /^\/(\S*)$/.exec(value)
+   if (!match) return []
+   const query = match[1].toLowerCase()
+   return SLASH_COMMANDS.filter(command => command.name.startsWith(query))
+ }

**The restart problem is fixed.** `yarn dev` now runs `electron-vite dev --watch` (commit `7de620b`, landed a few minutes ago while I was reading the code, so credit goes to whichever agent got there first). What that gives you:

- Renderer changes (React, Tailwind, anything in `src/renderer`) hot reload instantly, no restart
- Main and preload changes rebuild and restart Electron on their own

So the model picker Codex just added would have appeared without you touching anything. You need to quit and reopen **one** last time, because the dev script itself changed and the running process is still on the old one. After that you should not have to again.

**The pull and push buttons you asked for already exist.** They are in the top bar, in the rounded pill on the right:

- Down arrow: `git pull`
- Up arrow: `git push`
- Clicking the status text ("2 changes", "Up to date") opens a diff review of your local changes with its own Push button

That is `src/renderer/src/components/RepoControls.tsx:171-192`. It also polls every 10 seconds on its own, so the status dot updates without you doing anything. If you were not seeing it, it may have been hidden at a narrow window width, since the label text collapses under 1050px and only the dot stays.

**One gap worth knowing about.** Watch mode reloads code, but it cannot install packages. If someone's change adds a new dependency, the app will restart and then fail on a missing module until you run `yarn install`. Want me to add a notice in that pill that tells you when a pull brought in dependency changes? It is a small addition and it is the only case left where you have to do something manually.

That “1 change” should be inspectable, not just a number. I’ll make the change count open a clear review view with the changed files and their diff, so you can check exactly what changed before choosing Push. I’m using the high-end visual design skill again to keep that review flow consistent with the existing crew UI.
The count is currently only a status label, so there is no way to inspect what it represents. I’m wiring that label into a review popover now. It will list each local file, show added and removed lines, and expand the actual diff before Push. Runtime files such as `.crew/chat.jsonl` will be named plainly too, so persistent session activity is no longer a mystery change.
I also found why the indicator often sits at “1 change.” Sending a message updates `.crew/chat.jsonl`, then crew syncs it a moment later while the top bar is still showing the older count. Done. `/plan` is in, end to end, and `yarn tsc --noEmit` plus the full suite (271 tests) pass.

**How it works**

Type `/` in the chat composer and a command menu pops up with `/plan` (same feel as the `@` menu, arrow keys and Enter or Tab to pick). Then:

```
@Claude /plan add a dark theme
```

The `/plan` token can sit anywhere in the line. If only one agent is in the session you can drop the mention and it goes to them. With several agents and no mention, crew asks you to pick one.

That opens a thread in **plan mode**: the agent is told to read the project and write the plan, and not to touch any files. When it replies, the reply becomes the plan.

**In chat** the thread turns into a plan card instead of the usual thread card: the title, the plan itself rendered as markdown (clipped with a scrim), then a bar with **Implement plan**, **Open**, and a note that you open it to ask for changes. Asking another agent to rework the plan is just replying in the thread with `@name ...`, and the next plan they write replaces it.

**In the thread** the plan sits in a panel on the right while the run streams in the middle, with **Implement plan** pinned at the bottom. Press it and the thread leaves plan mode: the agent gets "Implement the plan." with the plan carried in as the brief, so it survives even a host restart.

**What changed**

- `src/shared/plan.ts` (new) — command parsing, the menu list, plan instructions
- `src/shared/events.ts`, `protocol.ts` — `ThreadMode`, `thread.plan` and `thread.implement` events, `plan.implement` message
- `src/server/session.ts` — plan threads, capturing the reply as the plan, plan framing in the prompt, the implement handler, replay on restart
- `src/renderer/src/components/SlashCommands.tsx`, `PlanCard.tsx`, `PlanPanel.tsx` (new), wired into `Chat.tsx` and `ThreadView.tsx`, plus store state
- `tests/plan.integration.test.ts`, `tests/plan-card-probe.test.ts` (new)

Two notes on choices I made, easy to change if you meant otherwise. Inside an open thread `/plan` stays plain text, since the command is for starting work rather than steering it. And the plan is kept on the thread rather than written to a doc page, so it stays next to the run it belongs to. Say the word if you want it saved into Docs as well.

**How it works** (`src/main/locate.ts`, new): every path an agent prints gets placed into one of three buckets, and the renderer draws it accordingly.

| Case | Shown as |
|---|---|
| Inside your project folder | relative, `src/renderer/src/App.tsx`, clickable |
| Another machine's copy of the project | same relative path (matched by path tail, so Ali's `/Users/ali/dev/crew/src/app.ts` opens your `src/app.ts`) |
| Outside the project but on your computer | the path as written |
| Someone else's home folder | a `Private file` chip, the path never renders |

System paths like `/usr/bin/env` stay as they are, since they read the same on every machine.

**Where it applies**
- `fileLinks.tsx` now recognizes absolute and `~` paths, not just relative ones, and relabels them once the main process places them. This covers chat markdown and plain message text.
- Step rows run their detail line through the same pass, so Read and Edit steps stop showing the full path.
- `cli.ts` strips the working folder prefix from step details at the source, so the host's own runs are relative before they even reach the session.
- `statFile` over IPC became `locatePath`, one entry point for the whole question.

Not a new-versus-old split. Two separate gaps, and neither one was about message age.

**What was actually happening**

Chat text and markdown already resolve at render time, so old messages there were covered. But:

1. The changed-files card and the file rows inside step rows render `file.path` straight from the event payload. `FilePathLink` (`src/renderer/src/components/StepRow.tsx:9`) never called the placement pass at all, so those paths showed raw whether the message was five minutes or five days old. That is the card in your screenshot.
2. Nothing in the pipeline understood Windows paths. `locate.ts` used posix `path.isAbsolute`, so `C:\Users\Ali Hammoud\crew\...` was treated as a relative path and passed through untouched. That one also broke the chat-text case, which is why Ali's paths leaked everywhere.

There was a third: `cli.ts` stripped the working folder with a hardcoded `/`, so on Ali's machine `C:\Users\Ali Hammoud\crew` never matched `C:\Users\Ali Hammoud\crew\src\...` and the paths arrived absolute in the first place.

**What changed**

- `src/main/locate.ts` recognizes Windows drive and UNC paths, and posix paths seen from Windows. A path written for the other operating system can never resolve locally, so it goes straight to the tail-matching step: `C:\Users\Ali Hammoud\crew\src\app.ts` finds your `src/app.ts`. If it does not match the project and sits under someone's user folder, it becomes a `Private file` chip.
- `FilePathLink` now runs the same pass, so the changed-files card, the single-file step label, and the expanded file rows all show the relative path. Clicking opens the resolved path, so the viewer stops saying "This file is not in the project".
- `stripRoot` and `stripRootFromText` in `src/shared/files.ts` handle either separator and normalize what is left to forward slashes. `cli.ts` uses them for both step details and file paths.
- Extracted `useLocated` in `fileLinks.tsx` so text and path components share one resolution path.

This all runs at render, so old conversations are fixed too. Reopen the thread and the card should read `src/renderer/src/state/store.ts`.

**Verified**: `file-read`, `file-links-probe`, `cli-command`, `providers.integration`, `agents.integration` all pass (108 tests), `yarn tsc --noEmit` clean. I did not run the full suite, since the failures another agent's `src/runner/index.ts` work introduced are still in flight and would drown out the signal.

Two separate things are going on, and neither is provider auto-detection. Nothing seeds agents from installed CLIs anymore: `agentDefs` (src/main/session.ts:233) only returns what's in your saved `agents.json`.

**The duplicates come from the agent id being derived from your display name.**

`agentId()` (src/shared/llm.ts:125) is `ownerName/instanceId`. Your `.crew/session.json` right now:

```
jamel/kimi                → Kimi          jamel (dev)/kimi        → Kimi 2
jamel/claude              → Claude        jamel (dev)/claude      → Claude 3
jamel/codex               → Codex         jamel (dev)/codex       → Codex 2
jamel/grok                → Grok          jamel (dev)/grok        → Grok 2
jamel/2b7ab567…           → UsageKiller   jamel (dev)/2b7ab567…   → UsageKiller 2
jamel/7e2e6858…           → Claude Opus 5 jamel (dev)/7e2e6858…   → Claude Opus 5 3
```

Identical instanceIds on both sides. That is one machine, one `agents.json`, hosted under two different names. The moment you type "Jamel (dev)" instead of "Jamel", every local agent gets a brand new composite id, `registerAgent` sees an unknown id and makes a fresh agent, and `uniqueLabel` (src/server/session.ts:1908) appends " 2" because the old label is still taken. The old set never goes away because agents are persisted in `.crew/session.json`, which is committed and pushed, so every name anyone has ever hosted under lives in the pool forever as offline ghosts. Ali's set is separate but has the same legacy `ali/claude` id from the old seeding, so it collided with your "Claude" and became "Claude 2".

**The one real auto-create path is `adoptOwnAgents`** (src/runner/index.ts:307). On connect, the runner scans the snapshot for any offline agent whose id starts with your name, checks whether that CLI is installed, and silently re-registers it. It only matches on id, not provider plus label, so on a machine that already has its own defs it can bring back a second copy of the same thing. It was built deliberately (tests/agents.integration.test.ts:105) for the wiped-store case, but it does create agents nobody asked for.

**Fix I'd recommend:** mint the agent id once at creation and persist it in `agents.json`, so the id travels with the def instead of being recomputed from whatever name you typed. Owner stays a display field on the agent, rename is just a label change, and hosting under a new name reuses the same agents. Legacy `owner/provider` ids keep their existing string so nothing in history breaks. Then delete `adoptOwnAgents`, and prune the 9 ghost agents out of `.crew/session.json`.

Done. Picking a mention (Tab, Enter, or clicking a row) now always leaves you with a space and the caret sitting after it.

`src/renderer/src/components/MentionAutocomplete.tsx:46` — `pick` inserts the token, adds a single space (reusing the one already there if the mention was inserted mid-sentence, so you never get a double space), and records where the caret belongs. A layout effect at line 37 then focuses the textarea and puts the caret right after the space once the new value is committed, instead of leaving it wherever the browser or React's selection restore happened to drop it. Same path covers `#doc` mentions, and it applies everywhere the hook is used: chat, threads, tasks, design chat.

Tests: `tests/mention-pick-probe.test.ts` covers the tab pick, the click pick, a doc pick, and picking with text already after the caret (that last one is what caught the double space).

Two things worth knowing:

- `src/server/git.ts:29` had merge conflict markers committed on main, from a sync autostash gone wrong, not from this change. It broke `yarn tsc --noEmit` for everyone. I resolved it by keeping `this.stop()`, which clears both the debounce timer and the loop, over the stashed `clearInterval(this.loop)`.
- `yarn tsc --noEmit` is clean. The full parallel `yarn test` run showed 19 failing files, all timeouts under load; running with `--no-file-parallelism` gives 52 passed, 1 failed, and that last file passes on its own. So the suite is green, just load-sensitive as usual.

step.text:
I dug through the codebase. Short answer: yes, and you already have most of the hard parts. `BrowserPanel` + `BrowserTabView` give you a tabbed `<webview>` host with `webviewTag: true` already on. What's missing is process supervision and a second rendering path for apps that aren't a URL.

## The idea

Three rendering paths, one tab UI. Crew picks the path per app, you never think about it.

**Path A, web (webview).** Anything that serves HTTP: Vite, Next, Rails, Django, Express, Go. Crew runs the project's dev command, watches stdout for the URL it prints, and points a webview at it. Real time is free, the framework's own HMR does it. This covers most repos.

**Path B, Chromium/Electron (CDP screencast).** This is the crew-in-crew case. A webview can't render a native window, but an Electron app launched with `--remote-debugging-port=0` prints `DevTools listening on ws://...` to stderr. Connect to that over `ws` (already a dependency), call `Page.startScreencast`, and you get a stream of JPEG frames of the child app's renderer. Works for any Electron or Chromium app, no cooperation from the target needed.

**Path C, native mirror (desktopCapturer).** Universal fallback for SwiftUI, Tauri, Qt, a simulator. `desktopCapturer.getSources({types:['window']})` gives you the child's window as a MediaStream, rendered into a `<video>`. Real time, view only. Input forwarding would need a native module, so instead there's a "focus the real window" button.

Honest limits worth knowing up front: Path B captures the page, not native chrome (traffic lights, native menus, vibrancy). For crew, which is frameless with a custom title bar, that's nearly the whole app. Path C needs macOS Screen Recording permission and is view only.

**Real time for agents, not just you.** The preview should also be something an agent can see. A camera button drops the current frame into the composer as an image attachment (the attachment pipeline already handles images), plus an opt-in "attach preview after each run" per thread, plus a "preview crashed" surface that offers to send the stderr tail into the thread.

**Crew previewing crew has four specific hazards** the plan handles: the child Electron inherits `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` / `ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL` / `NODE_OPTIONS` from the parent and must have them scrubbed; the child would resume the saved session from `session.json` and start hosting from the same repo, fighting the parent's `.crew/` writes and grabbing port 2739; the parent's `GitSync` auto-commits underneath the child; and ports collide. Fixes are a `CREW_PREVIEW=1` env guard, a separate `--user-data-dir`, an optional git worktree, and always parsing the port from output instead of assuming.

## Plan

### Phase 1: web previews end to end

**1. `src/shared/preview.ts`** (new) — `PreviewApp` config type (`id`, `name`, `kind: 'web' | 'electron' | 'native'`, `command`, `cwd`, `env`, `url`, `readyPattern`, `worktree`), `PreviewStatus` (`idle | starting | ready | crashed`), `PreviewLogLine`, `PreviewFrame`. No dependencies, per the layout rule.

**2. `src/preview/config.ts`** (new module, electron-free like server/runner/shared) — read and write `.crew/preview.json`, and autodetect apps when it's absent: package.json `scripts.dev` / `scripts.start`, then `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `manage.py`, `Gemfile`. **3. `src/preview/urls.ts`** (new) — pure parsers: dev-server URL out of a log line (`Local:   http://localhost:5173/`, `Listening on :3000`, `Server running at ...`), and the DevTools websocket endpoint out of Electron's stderr. Pure functions, cheap to test.

**4. `src/preview/process.ts`** (new) — the supervisor. Spawns detached with a scrubbed env, kills by process group like `src/runner/providers/cli.ts` already does, keeps a ring buffer of the last N log lines, detects ready via `urls.ts`, restarts, and reports nonzero exits with the stderr tail.

**5. `src/preview/manager.ts`** (new) — one live preview per app id, holds config plus process plus status, emits status/log/frame events. Single entry point for the main process.

**6. `src/main/preview.ts`** (new) — electron glue only: IPC handlers (`preview:apps`, `preview:start`, `preview:stop`, `preview:restart`, `preview:snapshot`), forwards manager events to the renderer over `webContents.send`, and uses `webContents.capturePage` for webview snapshots.

**7. `src/main/index.ts`** — register those handlers next to the existing `repo:*` ones, and stop all previews in `before-quit`.

**8. `src/main/preload.ts` + `src/renderer/src/env.d.ts`** — add the bridge methods and their types alongside the existing ones.

**9. `src/renderer/src/state/preview.ts`** (new) — zustand store for apps, per-app status, logs, active frame. Mirrors the shape of `state/browser.ts`.

**10. `src/renderer/src/state/browser.ts`** — add `kind: 'preview'` to `BrowserTab` with an `appId` field, plus an `openPreview(appId)` action. Reusing the tab model means preview inherits the pills, the side panel, and the width handling for free.

**11. `src/renderer/src/components/PreviewView.tsx`** (new) — renders a webview for `kind: 'web'`, and later a canvas or video for the other paths. Same absolute-inset visibility trick `BrowserTabView` uses.

**12. `src/renderer/src/components/PreviewToolbar.tsx`** (new) — app picker (`Select`), start/stop/restart, reload, viewport size presets, snapshot to composer, logs toggle. Pills and `@heroicons/react` (`PlayIcon`, `StopIcon`, `ArrowPathIcon`, `CameraIcon`, `ComputerDesktopIcon`, `DevicePhoneMobileIcon`), `Tooltip` never `title`, status as a `Pill`.

**13. `src/renderer/src/components/PreviewLogs.tsx`** (new) — collapsible log pane under the view, `ink-800` sunken, tail-follows.

**14. `src/renderer/src/components/BrowserPanel.tsx`** — branch on the new tab kind for the toolbar row and the view, add the tab pill icon.

**15. `src/renderer/src/components/TopBar.tsx`** — a "Preview" action that opens the preview tab, next to the existing repo controls.

**16. Tests** — `tests/preview-config.test.ts` (autodetect and round-trip), `tests/preview-urls.test.ts` (parsers), `tests/preview-process.integration.test.ts` (boots a real fixture server script on loopback, asserts ready detection, log capture, restart, clean kill), `tests/preview-panel-probe.test.ts` (renders the panel with a preview tab).

### Phase 2: Electron and crew-in-crew

**17. `src/preview/cdp.ts`** (new) — minimal CDP client over `ws`: attach to the endpoint, list page targets, `Page.startScreencast` with frame acks, `Input.dispatch*` for mouse/keyboard/wheel, `Page.captureScreenshot`, `Browser.setWindowBounds` to park the real child window offscreen. Also subscribes to `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` so the previewed app's console lands in the same log pane.

**18. `src/preview/worktree.ts`** (new) — create/reuse/remove a git worktree for the current branch, built on the existing `src/shared/git.ts` helper, so the child app's writes stay out of the parent's auto-commit loop.

**19. `src/main/session.ts`** — guard `resume()` on `CREW_PREVIEW` so a child crew doesn't rejoin the saved session and fight over `.crew/` and port 2739.

**20. `src/preview/process.ts`** — extend for `kind: 'electron'`: inject `--remote-debugging-port=0`, scrub the inherited Electron env vars, pass `--user-data-dir` into a temp dir per preview.

**21. `src/renderer/src/components/PreviewView.tsx`** — add the canvas renderer and input forwarding for CDP frames.

**22. Tests** — `tests/preview-cdp.integration.test.ts` drives the client against a stub websocket server speaking CDP frames, so it runs without a browser. `tests/preview-worktree.integration.test.ts` against a real temp repo, matching how `gitsync.integration.test.ts` works today.

### Phase 3: native mirror and agent handoff

**23. `src/main/preview.ts`** — `desktopCapturer` source lookup by child pid, handed to the renderer as a source id.

**24. `src/renderer/src/components/PreviewView.tsx`** — `<video>` path via `getUserMedia` with `chromeMediaSourceId`, plus a "focus the real window" button since input can't be forwarded.

**25. `src/renderer/src/components/Composer.tsx`** — accept a snapshot handoff from the preview store into the existing attachment flow.

**26. `src/renderer/src/components/PreviewToolbar.tsx`** — the per-thread "attach preview after each run" toggle.

**27. `AGENTS.md`** — add `src/preview` to the Layout section with the same no-electron rule as server/runner/shared, and note that `.crew/preview.json` is the shared config agents can edit.

Worth spiking before phase 2 is committed: whether an offscreen Electron window keeps compositing frames for `Page.startScreencast`. If it doesn't, the child window stays visible on the desktop and the in-crew view is a mirror of it rather than a replacement. That changes the feel, not the architecture.

A later follow-up, not in this plan: streaming frames over the session websocket so remote crew members and their agents watch the host's running app. The CDP path already produces exactly the frames that would need, so it's an additive protocol change.

+ import source from 'emoji-datasource-twitter/emoji.json'
+ import sheetUrl from 'emoji-datasource-twitter/img/twitter/sheets-256/64.png'
+ 
+ interface SourceEmoji {
+   name: string
+   unified: string
+   short_name: string
+   short_names: string[]
+   sheet_x: number
+   sheet_y: number
+   category: string
+   sort_order: number
+   has_img_twitter: boolean
+ }
+ 
+ export interface EmojiEntry {
+   char: string
+   shortName: string
+   terms: string[]
+   x: number
+   y: number
+ }
+ 
+ export interface EmojiCategory {
+   id: string
+   label: string
+   icon: string
+   entries: EmojiEntry[]
+ }
+ 
+ export const SHEET_URL = sheetUrl
+ export const SHEET_GRID = 62
+ 
+ const CATEGORIES: Array<{ id: string; source: string; label: string; icon: string }> = [
+   { id: 'smileys', source: 'Smileys & Emotion', label: 'Smileys', icon: '😀' },
+   { id: 'people', source: 'People & Body', label: 'People', icon: '👋' },
+   { id: 'nature', source: 'Animals & Nature', label: 'Animals and nature', icon: '🐻' },
+   { id: 'food', source: 'Food & Drink', label: 'Food and drink', icon: '🍔' },
+   { id: 'activity', source: 'Activities', label: 'Activities', icon: '⚽' },
+   { id: 'travel', source: 'Travel & Places', label: 'Travel and places', icon: '🚗' },
+   { id: 'objects', source: 'Objects', label: 'Objects', icon: '💡' },
+   { id: 'symbols', source: 'Symbols', label: 'Symbols', icon: '🔣' },
+   { id: 'flags', source: 'Flags', label: 'Flags', icon: '🚩' }
+ ]
+ 
+ const toChar = (unified: string) =>
+   String.fromCodePoint(...unified.split('-').map(part => Number.parseInt(part, 16)))
+ 
+ const ordered = (source as unknown as SourceEmoji[])
+   .filter(item => item.has_img_twitter)
+   .sort((a, b) => a.sort_order - b.sort_order)
+ 
+ const byCategory = new Map<string, EmojiEntry[]>()
+ const byChar = new Map<string, EmojiEntry>()
+ 
+ for (const item of ordered) {
+   const entry: EmojiEntry = {
+     char: toChar(item.unified),
+     shortName: item.short_name,
+     terms: [...new Set([...item.short_names, ...item.name.toLowerCase().split(/[^a-z0-9+]+/)])].filter(Boolean),
+     x: item.sheet_x,
+     y: item.sheet_y
+   }
+   byChar.set(entry.char, entry)
+   const bucket = byCategory.get(item.category) ?? []
+   bucket.push(entry)
+   byCategory.set(item.category, bucket)
+ }
+ 
+ export const EMOJI_CATEGORIES: EmojiCategory[] = CATEGORIES.map(category => ({
+   id: category.id,
+   label: category.label,
+   icon: category.icon,
+   entries: byCategory.get(category.source) ?? []
+ }))
+ 
+ export function lookupEmoji(char: string): EmojiEntry | undefined {
+   return byChar.get(char)
+ }
+ 
+ export function searchEmoji(query: string, limit = 108): EmojiEntry[] {
+   const needle = query.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^:|:$/g, '')
+   if (!needle) return []
+   const ranked: Array<{ entry: EmojiEntry; rank: number }> = []
+   for (const entry of byChar.values()) {
+     let rank = 4
+     for (const term of entry.terms) {
+       if (term === needle) rank = Math.min(rank, 0)
+       else if (term.startsWith(needle)) rank = Math.min(rank, term === entry.shortName ? 1 : 2)
+       else if (term.includes(needle)) rank = Math.min(rank, 3)
+     }
+     if (rank < 4) ranked.push({ entry, rank })
+     if (ranked.length > limit * 6) break
+   }
+   return ranked
+     .sort((a, b) => a.rank - b.rank)
+     .slice(0, limit)
+     .map(item => item.entry)
+ }
+

+ export function mentionsIn(
+   text: string,
+   agents: Array<Pick<PooledAgent, 'id' | 'label' | 'status'>>
+ ): string[] {
+   let work = ` ${text.toLowerCase()} `
+   const ids: string[] = []
+   const ordered = [...agents].sort((a, b) => b.label.length - a.label.length)
+   for (const agent of ordered) {
+     if (agent.status === 'offline') continue
+     const needle = `@${agent.label.toLowerCase()}`
+     const at = work.indexOf(needle)
+     if (at === -1) continue
+     if (/[\w-]/.test(work[at + needle.length])) continue
+     ids.push(agent.id)
+     work = work.slice(0, at) + ' '.repeat(needle.length) + work.slice(at + needle.length)
+   }
+   return ids
+ }
+ 
+ // What a written mention pointed at: the agent's id, plus the name it went out
+ // under. The id is what the mention means, the name is only how it was spelled.
+ export interface AgentMentionRef {
+   id: string
+   label: string
+ }
+ 
+ export function agentMentionRefsIn(
+   text: string,
+   agents: Array<Pick<PooledAgent, 'id' | 'label' | 'status'>>
+ ): AgentMentionRef[] {
+   const labels = new Map(agents.map(agent => [agent.id, agent.label]))
+   return mentionsIn(text, agents).map(id => ({ id, label: labels.get(id)! }))
+ }
+ 
+ function replaceMention(text: string, from: string, to: string): string {
+   const needle = from.toLowerCase()
+   let out = ''
+   let rest = text
+   for (;;) {
+     const at = rest.toLowerCase().indexOf(`@${needle}`)
+     if (at === -1) return out + rest
+     const end = at + needle.length + 1
+     if (/[\w-]/.test(rest[end] ?? '')) {
+       out += rest.slice(0, end)
+       rest = rest.slice(end)
+       continue
+     }
+     out += `${rest.slice(0, at)}@${to}`
+     rest = rest.slice(end)
+   }
+ }
+ 
+ // Brings written mentions up to date. A mention still means the agent it was
+ // aimed at, so a rename rewrites every "@old name" that pointed there.
+ export function relabelMentions(
+   text: string,
+   refs: AgentMentionRef[] | undefined,
+   agents: Array<Pick<PooledAgent, 'id' | 'label'>>
+ ): string {
+   if (!refs?.length) return text
+   let out = text
+   for (const ref of refs) {
+     const agent = agents.find(a => a.id === ref.id)
+     if (!agent || agent.label === ref.label) continue
+     out = replaceMention(out, ref.label, agent.label)
+   }
+   return out
+ }

+ // Brings written mentions up to date. A mention still means the agent it was
+ // aimed at, so a rename rewrites every "@old name" that pointed there. Names
+ // are swapped in one pass: two agents can trade names, and a rewritten mention
+ // must not be rewritten again by the next rename in the list.
+ export function relabelMentions(
+   text: string,
+   refs: AgentMentionRef[] | undefined,
+   agents: Array<Pick<PooledAgent, 'id' | 'label'>>
+ ): string {
+   if (!refs?.length) return text
+   const renames = new Map<string, string>()
+   for (const ref of refs) {
+     const agent = agents.find(a => a.id === ref.id)
+     if (!agent || agent.label === ref.label) continue
+     renames.set(ref.label.toLowerCase(), agent.label)
+   }
+   if (renames.size === 0) return text
+   const ordered = [...renames.keys()].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)
+   let out = ''
+   let rest = text
+   outer: for (;;) {
+     const lower = rest.toLowerCase()
+     for (let at = 0; at < rest.length; at++) {
+       if (lower[at] !== '@') continue
+       for (const old of ordered) {
+         if (!lower.startsWith(old, at + 1)) continue
+         const end = at + old.length + 1
+         if (/[\w-]/.test(rest[end] ?? '')) continue
+         out += `${rest.slice(0, at)}@${renames.get(old)}`
+         rest = rest.slice(end)
+         continue outer
+       }
+     }
+     return out + rest
+   }
+ }

step.text:
# Plan

Build on the existing Design workspace rather than replacing it. The current implementation already provides saved boards, real-time shape syncing, human and agent cursors, styled nodes, inspectors, and board-linked agent threads.

“Figma parity” will cover the Figma Design editor experience: drawing, frames, pages, layers, assets, components, variables, auto layout, prototypes, comments, version history, export, multiplayer presence, inspect/code mode, and AI-assisted design and coding. It will not include Figma’s billing, organization administration, community marketplace, FigJam, Slides, or third-party plugin runtime.

## Interaction contract

| Control | Click behavior |
|---|---|
| Pointer | Select, move, resize, rotate, multi-select, deep-select, and enter groups. Its menu adds Move and Scale. |
| Frame | Creates a frame. Its menu contains Frame, Section, and Slice with `F`, `Shift+S`, and `S`. |
| Shape | Uses the last selected shape. Its menu contains Rectangle, Line, Arrow, Ellipse, Polygon, Star, and Image/video with the shortcuts shown in the reference. |
| Pen | Starts vector path editing. Its menu switches between Pen and Pencil. Enter closes a path, Escape cancels the current segment. |
| Text | Creates point text on click and fixed-width text on drag. |
| Comment | Places a comment pin and opens its thread. Mentions notify people inside the current crew session. |
| Resources | Opens Components, Styles, Variables, and Assets. Components can be dragged onto the canvas as instances. |
| Design mode | Shows layers and the complete design inspector. |
| Prototype mode | Shows interaction handles, connections, transitions, flows, and the presentation button. |
| Code mode | Shows inspect values and generated CSS, React, and Tailwind output. It can hand the selected frame to a coding agent. |
| Board title | Opens the board switcher. Double-click renames it. The menu supports create, duplicate, rename, and delete. |
| People | Shows humans and agents currently on the board. Clicking one follows their viewport. |
| Share | Copies the crew invite link and shows current session access. |
| Present | Opens a focused prototype preview starting from the selected flow. |
| Zoom | Opens zoom presets, zoom-to-fit, zoom-to-selection, rulers, pixel grid, and snap settings. |
| Right chat | Sends a task to one or more agents with Design, Code, or Design + code scope. |
| Agent log | Expands into thinking, tool calls, changed files, canvas operations, subagents, elapsed time, and token use. |
| Agent cursor | Uses `AgentIcon`, shows the current operation, and follows created or edited frames. |
| Generating frame | Shows “Generating screen…” above the frame with a subtle active outline until the run finishes. |

## Implementation order

1. [src/shared/design.ts](C:/Users/Ali%20Hammoud/crew/src/shared/design.ts)

   Expand the board model with pages, revisions, comments, named versions, prototype flows, shared styles, variables, assets, and active agent activity. Extend presence with viewport, current tool, prompt ID, activity text, and followed user. Add backward-compatible defaults for existing saved boards.

2. [src/shared/designNode.ts](C:/Users/Ali%20Hammoud/crew/src/shared/designNode.ts)

   Extend design nodes with visibility, locking, opacity, constraints, independent strokes, image fills, advanced gradients, typography details, resizing rules, auto-layout wrapping, absolute children, component definitions, instances, variants, property overrides, variable bindings, and export settings.

3. `src/shared/designPrototype.ts`

   Add typed prototype flows, triggers, actions, destinations, overlays, scrolling behavior, transitions, easing, and presentation settings.

4. `src/shared/designLibrary.ts`

   Define reusable components, variants, color styles, text styles, effect styles, grids, and local variables. Include helpers for resolving instance overrides and variable aliases.

5. [src/shared/protocol.ts](C:/Users/Ali%20Hammoud/crew/src/shared/protocol.ts)

   Add messages for revision-aware document changes, page metadata, comments, versions, library changes, prototype changes, agent canvas activity, viewport following, and resync requests. Preserve support for older clients using the existing design messages.

6. [src/server/store.ts](C:/Users/Ali%20Hammoud/crew/src/server/store.ts)

   Upgrade `.crew/designs/` persistence to store the current document, comments, library data, prototype data, and named version snapshots. Add migration from the existing single JSON board format. Store imported canvas media through the existing attachment system so assets remain synced through git.

7. [src/server/designops.ts](C:/Users/Ali%20Hammoud/crew/src/server/designops.ts)

   Extend the agent operation API to create and update pages, sections, slices, vectors, images, components, instances, variants, styles, variables, prototype links, and comments. Return the new revision and affected frame IDs after every batch.

8. [src/server/nodeops.ts](C:/Users/Ali%20Hammoud/crew/src/server/nodeops.ts)

   Validate the expanded node properties, resolve variable references, enforce component-instance rules, and reject invalid parent, page, and prototype references without corrupting the board.

9. [src/server/session.ts](C:/Users/Ali%20Hammoud/crew/src/server/session.ts)

   Make the host authoritative for board revisions. Apply operations in order, request resync after gaps, and broadcast agent activity separately from persisted document data. Add comment threads, version creation and restore, follow mode, page-aware presence, and clean disconnect behavior. Associate active board prompts with agent canvas operations so the UI can show which frame each agent is changing.

10. [src/server/index.ts](C:/Users/Ali%20Hammoud/crew/src/server/index.ts)

I’m using the high-end visual design skill to keep the Figma-style workspace consistent with crew’s existing visual system. I’ll inspect the five references and the current renderer, collaboration protocol, and agent flow, then return a file-by-file implementation plan only.
The references resolve into three connected surfaces: a Figma-like floating tool island with nested menus, a zoomable multiplayer canvas with live cursors and frames, and a Stitch-style AI run card with progress plus an expandable agent log. I’m mapping those onto crew’s existing room and agent architecture now so the plan extends current behavior instead of proposing a separate app.
The codebase already has a strong starting point: live tldraw document sync, multiplayer cursors, board persistence, an agent HTTP design API, real styled design nodes, a basic inspector, and board-linked chat threads. The plan will replace the current generic canvas chrome and fill the missing Figma layers, assets, prototype, history, comments, export, and agent-run workflow rather than rebuilding sync from scratch.
# Plan

Build on the existing Design workspace rather than replacing it. The current implementation already provides saved boards, real-time shape syncing, human and agent cursors, styled nodes, inspectors, and board-linked agent threads.

“Figma parity” will cover the Figma Design editor experience: drawing, frames, pages, layers, assets, components, variables, auto layout, prototypes, comments, version history, export, multiplayer presence, inspect/code mode, and AI-assisted design and coding. It will not include Figma’s billing, organization administration, community marketplace, FigJam, Slides, or third-party plugin runtime.

## Interaction contract

| Control | Click behavior |
|---|---|
| Pointer | Select, move, resize, rotate, multi-select, deep-select, and enter groups. Its menu adds Move and Scale. |
| Frame | Creates a frame. Its menu contains Frame, Section, and Slice with `F`, `Shift+S`, and `S`. |
| Shape | Uses the last selected shape. Its menu contains Rectangle, Line, Arrow, Ellipse, Polygon, Star, and Image/video with the shortcuts shown in the reference. |
| Pen | Starts vector path editing. Its menu switches between Pen and Pencil. Enter closes a path, Escape cancels the current segment. |
| Text | Creates point text on click and fixed-width text on drag. |
| Comment | Places a comment pin and opens its thread. Mentions notify people inside the current crew session. |
| Resources | Opens Components, Styles, Variables, and Assets. Components can be dragged onto the canvas as instances. |
| Design mode | Shows layers and the complete design inspector. |
| Prototype mode | Shows interaction handles, connections, transitions, flows, and the presentation button. |
| Code mode | Shows inspect values and generated CSS, React, and Tailwind output. It can hand the selected frame to a coding agent. |
| Board title | Opens the board switcher. Double-click renames it. The menu supports create, duplicate, rename, and delete. |
| People | Shows humans and agents currently on the board. Clicking one follows their viewport. |
| Share | Copies the crew invite link and shows current session access. |
| Present | Opens a focused prototype preview starting from the selected flow. |
| Zoom | Opens zoom presets, zoom-to-fit, zoom-to-selection, rulers, pixel grid, and snap settings. |
| Right chat | Sends a task to one or more agents with Design, Code, or Design + code scope. |
| Agent log | Expands into thinking, tool calls, changed files, canvas operations, subagents, elapsed time, and token use. |
| Agent cursor | Uses `AgentIcon`, shows the current operation, and follows created or edited frames. |
| Generating frame | Shows “Generating screen…” above the frame with a subtle active outline until the run finishes. |

+ import { RefObject, useEffect, useState } from 'react'
+ 
+ export default function useScrollEdges(ref: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>) {
+   const [edges, setEdges] = useState({ top: true, bottom: true })
+ 
+   const update = () => {
+     const el = ref.current
+     if (!el) return
+     const top = el.scrollTop < 2
+     const bottom = el.scrollTop + el.clientHeight > el.scrollHeight - 2
+     setEdges(prev => (prev.top === top && prev.bottom === bottom ? prev : { top, bottom }))
+   }
+ 
+   useEffect(update)
+ 
+   useEffect(() => {
+     const el = ref.current
+     if (!el) return
+     el.addEventListener('scroll', update)
+     return () => el.removeEventListener('scroll', update)
+   }, [ref])
+ 
+   return { edges, update }
+ }
+

step.text:
Done. You can now upload a photo for any agent you own under Crew, and taking it off brings back the generated pet.

How it works:

- **Crew tab** (`src/renderer/src/components/AgentPhoto.tsx`): hovering an agent's icon shows a photo button. With no photo it opens the file picker straight away; with one it opens a small menu with "Change photo" and "Remove photo". The control only appears on agents you own, same as rename.
- **The image** goes to the host over the socket (`agent.avatar`), lands in `.crew/attachments` through the same path chat images use, and the file name is stored on the agent in `session.json`, so it survives restarts and syncs to everyone through git.
- **AgentIcon** (`src/renderer/src/components/AgentIcon.tsx:105`) looks the photo up by agent id, so the picture shows everywhere the agent appears: chat, threads, mentions, the picker. With no photo it draws the generated icon exactly as before, and since that icon is derived from the agent id, removing a photo puts back the same one the agent always had.
- Only the owner can set it, and anything that is not a png, jpg, gif or webp under 10MB is turned away.

Tests: `tests/agent-avatar.integration.test.ts` (upload, remove, persistence, refusals) and `tests/agent-photo-probe.test.ts` (the Crew tab UI, including landing back on the generated icon). Both pass, and `yarn tsc --noEmit` is clean.

One thing worth knowing: a full `yarn test` run shows failures in `emoji-picker`, `repo-controls`, `home-recent-probe` and `agent-ownership`. I checked those against an older commit in a scratch worktree and they fail there too, so they predate this change. The rest of the suite passes when run serially.

+ import { useCallback, useRef, useState } from 'react'
+ import { hoverCardOpen } from './HoverCard'
+ 
+ // Hysteresis: rubber-band bounce at the bottom must not unpin, and a deliberate
+ // upward scroll must never have to outrun the streaming auto-scroll.
+ const UNPIN_SLOP = 12
+ const REPIN_DISTANCE = 60
+ 
+ type Remembered = { top: number; pinned: boolean }
+ 
+ const remembered = new Map<string, Remembered>()
+ 
+ /**
+  * Tracks whether the user is pinned to the bottom of a scroll container.
+  * Scrolling up past a small threshold unpins (auto-scroll stops fighting the
+  * user); scrolling back into the bottom re-pins. Reads direction from scroll
+  * events, so programmatic scrolls to the bottom never unpin.
+  *
+  * Pass a key to remember where the user was across unmounts, so leaving a view
+  * and coming back lands in the same place. A view that was pinned re-pins to
+  * the bottom instead, since messages may have arrived while it was gone.
+  */
+ export function useStickToBottom(scrollRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>, memoryKey?: string) {
+   const pinnedRef = useRef(true)
+   const [scrolledUp, setScrolledUp] = useState(false)
+   const lastScrollTop = useRef(0)
+   const restored = useRef(false)
+ 
+   const setPinned = useCallback((pinned: boolean) => {
+     pinnedRef.current = pinned
+     setScrolledUp(!pinned)
+   }, [])
+ 
+   const onScroll = useCallback(() => {
+     const el = scrollRef.current
+     if (!el) return
+     const distance = el.scrollHeight - el.scrollTop - el.clientHeight
+     const up = el.scrollTop < lastScrollTop.current
+     if (up && distance > UNPIN_SLOP) setPinned(false)
+     else if (!up && distance <= REPIN_DISTANCE) setPinned(true)
+     lastScrollTop.current = el.scrollTop
+     if (memoryKey) remembered.set(memoryKey, { top: el.scrollTop, pinned: pinnedRef.current })
+   }, [memoryKey, scrollRef, setPinned])
+ 
+   const jumpToBottom = useCallback(() => {
+     const el = scrollRef.current
+     if (!el) return
+     setPinned(true)
+     el.scrollTo({ top: el.scrollHeight, behavior: 'smooth' })
+   }, [scrollRef, setPinned])
+ 
+   const follow = useCallback(
+     (ready = true) => {
+       const el = scrollRef.current
+       if (!el) return
+       if (restored.current) {
+         if (pinnedRef.current && !hoverCardOpen()) el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight
+         return
+       }
+       if (!ready) return
+       restored.current = true
+       const saved = memoryKey ? remembered.get(memoryKey) : undefined
+       if (saved && !saved.pinned) {
+         setPinned(false)
+         lastScrollTop.current = saved.top
+         el.scrollTop = saved.top
+         return
+       }
+       el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight
+     },
+     [memoryKey, scrollRef, setPinned]
+   )
+ 
+   return { pinnedRef, scrolledUp, onScroll, jumpToBottom, follow }
+ }
+

Done. The tab tooltips now only appear when the nav collapses to icons.

**What changed**

- `src/renderer/src/components/TopBar.tsx` — the header watches its own width with a `ResizeObserver` and passes `disabled={!compact}` to the tab `Tooltip`s. `COMPACT_WIDTH` is 760, matching the container query in `styles.css:199` that hides `.top-bar-tab-label`. So at full width, where the labels are already on screen, hovering a tab shows nothing. The Tasks button keeps its tooltip since it is icon-only at every width.
- `tests/top-bar-responsive.test.ts` — new case asserting no tooltip at 1200px and a tooltip at 600px.
- `tests/repo-controls.test.ts` — added the same `TestResizeObserver` stub the other jsdom probes use, since it renders `TopBar`.

**Checks**

`yarn tsc --noEmit` clean. The top bar, repo controls, plan card, and thread view suites pass.

Two things to flag on the full `yarn test` run: `emoji-picker` and `home-recent-probe` fail on `localStorage` being undefined under this Node build (it prints `localStorage is not available because --localstorage-file was not provided`), and the integration suites each drop one `waitFor` timeout when all 59 files run together. Both are pre-existing and unrelated to this change. `queue.integration.test.ts` passes on its own.

+ import { desktopCapturer, shell, systemPreferences, type Session } from 'electron'
+ 
+ export type MediaKind = 'microphone' | 'camera' | 'screen'
+ export type MediaAccess = 'granted' | 'denied' | 'restricted' | 'unknown'
+ 
+ export interface ScreenSource {
+   id: string
+   name: string
+   kind: 'screen' | 'window'
+   thumbnail: string
+   icon: string | null
+ }
+ 
+ const THUMBNAIL = { width: 640, height: 400 }
+ const ICON = { width: 32, height: 32 }
+ 
+ const SETTINGS_PANES: Record<MediaKind, string> = {
+   microphone: 'x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Microphone',
+   camera: 'x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Camera',
+   screen: 'x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture'
+ }
+ 
+ // The chosen source is handed over just before the renderer asks for the
+ // stream, so the request handler answers without a second round trip.
+ let pending: string | null = null
+ 
+ export function pickScreenSource(id: string | null): void {
+   pending = typeof id === 'string' && id ? id : null
+ }
+ 
+ export function installDisplayMedia(session: Session): void {
+   session.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler((_request, callback) => {
+     const wanted = pending
+     pending = null
+     if (!wanted) {
+       callback({})
+       return
+     }
+     desktopCapturer
+       .getSources({ types: ['screen', 'window'] })
+       .then(sources => {
+         const source = sources.find(s => s.id === wanted)
+         callback(source ? { video: source } : {})
+       })
+       .catch(() => callback({}))
+   })
+ }
+ 
+ export function mediaAccess(kind: MediaKind): MediaAccess {
+   if (process.platform !== 'darwin') return 'granted'
+   const status = systemPreferences.getMediaAccessStatus(kind)
+   if (status === 'granted' || status === 'denied' || status === 'restricted') return status
+   return 'unknown'
+ }
+ 
+ export async function askForMedia(kind: 'microphone' | 'camera'): Promise<boolean> {
+   if (process.platform !== 'darwin') return true
+   if (systemPreferences.getMediaAccessStatus(kind) === 'granted') return true
+   return systemPreferences.askForMediaAccess(kind)
+ }
+ 
+ // Screen recording is the one permission macOS will not let an app ask for, so
+ // the app opens the pane and the person turns it on themselves.
+ export function openMediaSettings(kind: MediaKind): void {
+   if (process.platform !== 'darwin') return
+   void shell.openExternal(SETTINGS_PANES[kind])
+ }
+ 
+ export async function screenSources(): Promise<ScreenSource[]> {
+   const sources = await desktopCapturer.getSources({
+     types: ['screen', 'window'],
+     thumbnailSize: THUMBNAIL,
+     fetchWindowIcons: true
+   })
+   return sources
+     .filter(source => !source.thumbnail.isEmpty())
+     .map(source => ({
+       id: source.id,
+       name: source.name,
+       kind: source.id.startsWith('screen:') ? ('screen' as const) : ('window' as const),
+       thumbnail: source.thumbnail.toDataURL(),
+       icon: source.appIcon && !source.appIcon.isEmpty() ? source.appIcon.resize(ICON).toDataURL() : null
+     }))
+ }
+
